papers.title: Tribological Behavior of Ti-6Al-4V Alloys Processed by Selective Laser Melting and Conventional Casting Process
papers.abstract: This work presents a detailed assessment of the microstructural features and tribological behaviour of Ti6Al4V alloy produced by conventional casting followed by rolling (CR) and selective laser melting (SLM). The two fabrication routes yield markedly different microstructures: the CR alloy develops a dualphase α + β microstructure, whereas the SLM alloy forms a fine martensitic α′ lath morphology with enhanced hardness. Tribological experiments performed under various loads and sliding speeds reveal clear distinctions in frictional response and wear characteristics. The CR samples exhibit deeper ploughing grooves, stronger oxidation effects, and higher coefficients of friction, indicating that abrasive and oxidationassisted wear dominate their surface degradation. In contrast, the SLM samples show shallower wear tracks, reduced friction, and improved resistance to material removal, with delamination and adhesive wear occurring only under more severe test conditions. The lower COF and diminished wear severity observed in the SLM alloy highlight the advantages of its refined microstructure in stabilizing interfacial contact and reducing frictional energy losses. Overall, the results confirm the superior tribological performance of SLMprocessed Ti6Al4V for applications demanding high wear resistance and structural reliability.

papers.title: Mission-aware Model Predictive Control for tactical microgrids under monsoon uncertainty
papers.abstract: Tactical microgrids in remote and mission-critical environments must ensure reliable power, reduce fuel use, and maintain acoustic stealth under uncertain renewable generation. However, most existing control strategies are either rule-based or single-objective, which limits their ability to handle these conflicting goals in real time.This paper proposes a mission-aware Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for a hybrid PV–battery–diesel microgrid. The approach directly embeds mission priorities into the dispatch problem using a rolling-horizon optimization. A key novelty is the Survival Override mechanism, which protects battery reserves under solar forecast uncertainty and helps prevent mission failure.The framework is validated through co-simulation using Python and DIgSILENT PowerFactory with realistic solar data. The results show a 61.9% reduction in fuel consumption compared to conventional control. At the same time, the system maintains voltage stability and supports up to 20 hours of continuous silent operation. The controller also handles forecast errors of up to 15% through 15-minute receding horizon updates, avoiding early battery depletion and inefficient generator use.Overall, the proposed approach improves microgrid resilience, reduces fuel logistics, and enhances operational performance without requiring additional system capacity.

papers.title: M300-C18150 bimetal 3D printing by laser powder bed fusion: effect of process parameters on single track and layer development
papers.abstract: Abstract Powder Bed Fusion of metals using laser beam (PBF-LB/M) relies on stable single-track and single-layer deposition to produce dense, and defect-free components, a requirement that is particularly challenging in bimetallic systems with dissimilar thermophysical properties. This study investigated the effects of PBF-LB/M process parameters on single-track and single-layer deposition in a bimetallic system comprising M300 maraging steel and C18150 copper alloy. An SLM 280 2.0 2MA PBF-LB/M machine equipped with twin 700 W IPG Ytterbium fiber lasers was used to print the bimetal samples. Laser scan velocities (500–1100 mm/s), laser powers (300–550 W), and hatch spacings (0.08–0.14 mm) were systematically varied for deposition of M300 on C18150 substrates and vice versa. Surface integrity was quantified using surface roughness parameters (Ra and Sa), while melt pool geometry and interfacial characteristics were analysed using optical and scanning electron microscopy. For single tracks of M300 deposited on C18150, increasing scan velocity led to higher surface roughness and reduced melt pool width and depth, whereas higher laser power increased melt pool dimensions. In contrast, single tracks of C18150 deposited on M300 exhibited discontinuous tracks, high variability in melt pool geometry, and unstable deposition behaviour. Single-layer results revealed smoother surfaces for M300 on C18150 under low scan velocity, 500–700 mm/s, small hatch spacing, 0.08–0.1 mm and high laser power, 400–450 W. The reverse configuration, C18150 on M300, however, rendered better surface quality at the same velocity and hatch space ranges but at higher power, 500–550 W. The lowest surface roughness (Ra = 15.7 ± 1.9 μm; Sa = 19.9 ± 0.4 μm ) was for M300 on C18150 configuration and for C18150 on M300 (Ra = 14.9 ± 7.1 μm; Sa = 48 ± 16 μm). Interfacial analysis showed material intermixing in both configurations, with more pronounced defect formation when depositing C18150 on M300. Overall, the results of this study provide critical insights into the process–structure relationships governing bimetallic PBF-LB/M fabrication and contribute to the advancement of parameter optimisation strategies for the production of structurally sound bimetallic components.

papers.title: INFECTION FOLLOWING LOWER LIMB TRANSFEMORAL AND TRANSTIBIAL OSSEOINTEGRATION SURGERY: A SINGLE-CENTRE RETROSPECTIVE REVIEW
papers.abstract: Lower limb osseointegration (OI) surgery is a novel surgical procedure performed on patients with lower extremity amputations at a limited number of US centers. Traditional socket-based prostheses can negatively impact quality of life and carry many functional restrictions. The OI surgical procedure is performed in one or two stages, which involves implanting a stem into either the femur or tibia depending on the level of the amputation, and the creation of a stoma through which the external prosthesis attaches to said stem. The stoma lacks a physiologic skin seal and creates a portal of entry for bacteria directly to the underlying osseous structures, soft tissue, and implant. As such, infection rates for osseointegration surgeries outpace those of other orthopaedic surgical procedures. More information is needed regarding the microbiological profile of these infections, infection-related outcomes, and risk factors for these patient cohorts. Our study aims to describe the microbiology and clinical characteristics of lower limb OI infections, to assess outcomes in those with lower limb OI infections, and assess if pre-operative antibiotic choice predisposes to OI related lower limb infection. An institutional review board (IRB) approved retrospective analysis was performed on all patients who underwent either transtibial or transfemoral lower limb osseointegration surgery at our institution from September 16th, 2019 through September 12th, 2024. Demographic, medical, operative, and outcomes data were collected for all patients in the cohort. Twenty-six infection events occurred in twenty-four unique patients out of eighty-one total patients who met inclusion criteria, for an infection rate of 29.6%. Patients were followed for a minimum of twelve months, with a range of follow up from 12 to 71.9 months. Twelve infection events were monomicrobial (46.1%), and seventeen (65.4%) had gram positive organisms only. The most common type of infection was skin and soft tissue or stoma-related, with eleven (42.3%). Nineteen (73.1%) infection events required a return trip to the operating room. Twenty-three events (88.5%) maintained retention of the osseointegrated implant. This study helps to advance the knowledge base surrounding osseointegrated lower limb implant infections and describes the predominantly gram-positive microbiological characteristics and outcomes of those infections. Though there is a high infection rate, the outcomes are generally good with a high implant retention rate. Additionally, we found that the use of appropriate pre operative anti-microbials with cefazolin is protective against developing infection. Finally, this study highlights the need for multi-disciplinary management of these patients.

papers.title: On brittle fracture analysis of architected materials using a structural-level frame model
papers.abstract: This study proposes a mesoscale model for the deformation and fracture of lattice-frame based architected structures. It is directly based on moment-curvature and stress-strain relationships of the individual frame elements, augmented by thermodynamically consistent fracture propagation criteria. By modeling dense frames directly and introducing two fracture probability parameters (for tensile and bending fracture), we are able to capture a wide variety of fracture behavior of architected lattice structures. The model is applied to study the fracture behavior of various two-dimensional lattice structures under different load conditions. The model demonstrates that the nature of the failure of architected materials is very sensitive to mesostructure, as expected. It is also able to capture the quasi-brittle post-failure softening behavior that is observed even though the material of the lattice is brittle. The results show that, depending upon the lattice structure, the local bending moment distribution (or local curvature distribution) can be very widespread, thus promoting quasi-brittle behavior. The framework is computationally efficient and accounts for the local discrete mesostructure that is not captured by classical continua. The present work is intended as a methodological framework and proof-of-concept; results are interpreted in terms of qualitative trends and relative mesostructural comparisons, with experimental validation identified as a direction for future work.

papers.title: Minor Deviations in Cup Center of Rotation Can Reduce Impingement-Free Range of Motion in Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background Precise restoration of the acetabular center of rotation (COR) is important for hip biomechanics, particularly in patients with stiff spinopelvic mobility. This study quantified the effect of small COR shifts on impingement-free virtual range of motion (ROM). Methods We retrospectively reviewed the final acetabular component position achieved during robotically assisted total hip arthroplasty in 100 patients. Impingement-free ROM was measured for the final plan, then reassessed after translating the COR 2 mm anteriorly, superiorly, or medially. Patients were stratified by spinopelvic flexibility. Results A 2 mm COR shift altered virtual ROM in 93% of patients. Medial translation increased failure to meet any functional ROM threshold from 16% to 30% ( P < .001). Stiff-spined patients showed significantly higher failure rates after all COR shifts ( P < .05). Conclusions Small deviations from planned COR meaningfully reduce virtual ROM and have the greatest impact in patients with stiff spinopelvic mechanics.

papers.title: POSTOPERATIVE “PROPHYLACTIC” ORAL ANTIBIOTIC USE IS A MARKER FOR SUBSEQUENT INFECTION AFTER ASEPTIC REVISION TOTAL HIP ARTHROPLASTY
papers.abstract: Introduction & Aim Postoperative prophylactic oral antibiotics (PPOA) are variably used after aseptic revision total hip arthroplasty (rTHA), despite limited evidence of benefit. This study examined PPOA's link to periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), healthcare use, and antibiotic-related adverse events. Methods A retrospective study using a national claims database from 2016 to 2023 identified patients undergoing aseptic rTHA, who were grouped by PPOA exposure. PPOA was defined as a minimum duration of seven days of antibiotics between seven and 14 days post-surgery; controls had less than two days. Propensity score matching (1: 2) using demographics, comorbidities, procedure type, and healthcare factors, resulting in 840 PPOA patients and 1,677 controls. The primary outcome was PJI at one year; secondary outcomes included healthcare resource utilization, re- revision, and adverse events. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to adjust for potentially confounding variables and sensitivity analysis was performed to assess data robustness, excluding patients placed on early postoperative oral therapy for SSI, hematoma, UTI, and pneumonia. Results PPOA was associated with higher PJI rates at 90 days (2.1% vs 0.9%; OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.18–4.26; p = 0.018) and one year (2.9% vs 1.6%; OR 1.77, 95% CI 1.06–2.96; p = 0.039). PPOA was also associated with higher 30-day superficial SSI rates (6.7% vs 2.6%; OR 2.71; p < 0.001) and wound complication rates (3.3% vs 1.6%; OR 2.03, 95% CI 1.24–3.34; p = 0.006), but there was no difference in emergency department visits or readmissions. After excluding 198 patients with early postoperative infection or wound complications (e.g. SSI, hematoma, UTI, and pneumonia), PPOA remained associated with higher risk of recurrent infection at 90 days (aOR 2.09, p < 0.001), one year (aOR 1.86, p = 0.011), and two years (aOR 1.79, p = 0.002). Conclusions PPOA was not associated with reduced PJI, healthcare utilization, or re-revision. PPOA recipients had higher observed infection and wound complication rates, even after matching and sensitivity exclusions, likely reflecting unmeasured clinical risk rather than a causal effect of antibiotics. These findings do not support routine PPOA after aseptic rTHA and highlight the need to better define high-risk patients who may warrant selective antibiotic use.

papers.title: PREFORMULATED ANTIBIOFILM IRRIGATION DOES NOT IMPROVE OUTCOMES IN DAIR FOR ACUTE PERIPROSTHETIC JOINT INFECTION: A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL
papers.abstract: Aim To evaluate the clinical effectiveness of a preformulated antibiofilm irrigation solution compared with normal saline in patients with acute hip or knee periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) treated with debridement, antibiotics, irrigation, and implant retention (DAIR). Methods We conducted a single-centre randomized controlled trial including patients with acute postoperative or hematogenous hip or knee PJI treated with DAIR between December 2022 and December 2024. Patients were randomized (1:1) to irrigation with normal saline or a preformulated antibiofilm solution*. The primary endpoint was infection control at 12 months. Secondary objectives included analysis of failure patterns and identification of factors associated with treatment outcomes. The primary analysis followed a modified intention-to-treat (mITT) approach, including only patients with confirmed PJI and available follow-up. Results Of 56 patients initially enrolled, 48 were included in the final analysis (24 per group). Two patients were lost to follow-up due to deaths unrelated to PJI, and six were excluded because PJI diagnosis could not be confirmed according to predefined criteria. Baseline characteristics were comparable, except for a higher proportion of anticoagulant therapy in the group with a preformulated antibiofilm solution* (58.3% vs 25%; p=0.039). The overall success rate was 56.25% (27/48), with no significant difference between groups (saline 54.16% vs preformulated antibiofilm solution* 58.33%; p=1.000). Kaplan–Meier analysis showed that most failures occurred within the first six weeks after DAIR, with no differences between groups (p=0.638). No adverse events related to the preformulated antibiofilm solution* were identified. Primary total hip arthroplasty was independently associated with a lower risk of failure (OR 0.12; 95% CI 0.01–0.97; p=0.047). Among failures requiring repeat debridement, most recurrences were relapses with the same pathogen. Conclusions In this randomized controlled trial, the use of a preformulated antibiofilm irrigation solution did not improve infection control compared with normal saline in DAIR for acute or hematogenous PJI. Failures occurred early and were predominantly due to relapse with the initial pathogen. * Bactisure®

papers.title: Mid-Term Clinical, Radiographic, and Safety Outcomes After Hemiarthroplasty with the CL TRAUMA Cemented Femoral Stem: A Post-Market Clinical Investigation
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cemented femoral stems are a well-established treatment option for femoral neck fractures (FNFs) in elderly patients. This study evaluated mid-term clinical and radiographic outcomes and safety profile in patients undergoing hemiarthroplasty with the CL TRAUMA cemented femoral stem (LimaCorporate) for FNF. Methods: The single-center observational Post-Market Clinical Investigation identified 474 patients who underwent hip arthroplasty between 2017 and 2023. Of these, 54 (11.4%) who were alive, contactable, willing, and physically able to attend were included in the mid-term follow-up (FU) assessment. Perioperative, discharge, and 1-month FU data were collected retrospectively, while mid-term clinical and radiographic FU was performed prospectively after a minimum of 2 years. The primary endpoint was satisfactory status, defined as a Harris Hip Score (HHS) ≥ 80. Secondary endpoints included patient satisfaction assessed using Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), radiographic outcomes, and documented serious adverse events (SAEs). Results: The 54 evaluated patients (54/474; 11.4% of the implanted population) included 49 females and 5 males, with a mean age at surgery of 77.1 ± 9.1 years and a mean FU of 4.4 ± 0.8 years. All patients underwent hemiarthroplasty for FNF. Mean HHS was 80.6 ± 16.9, with 33 patients (61.1%) achieving the primary endpoint. Mean VAS satisfaction was 76.4 ± 29.3. At mid-term FU, RLLs were observed in 38.9% of patients, predominantly of limited thickness. Distal stem migration was observed in one case (1.9%), and bone remodeling in three patients (5.6%). Eleven SAEs occurred in 10 patients (18.5%); three events were related and two possibly related to the surgical procedure, whereas none was considered related to the device. No femoral stem revisions were documented among the 54 evaluated patients during the available FU. Conclusions: Among the selected patients who survived and completed mid-term follow-up after bipolar hemiarthroplasty with the CL TRAUMA cemented femoral stem, satisfactory functional status and patient satisfaction were observed, together with generally stable stem-specific radiographic findings. No SAEs were considered related to the femoral stem, and no femoral stem revisions were documented. These findings should be interpreted cautiously and cannot be extrapolated to the entire implanted population.

papers.title: Graded-twist TPMS metamaterial with twist-locking mechanism and non-monotonic stiffness
papers.abstract: Triply Periodic Minimal Surfaces (TPMS) are increasingly exploited in additively manufactured metamaterials due to their smooth, continuous topologies that enable unusual mechanical behaviours. This paper proposes a graded-twist TPMS structure that undergoes continuous rotation along the height direction, leveraging its continuous topology to introduce a spatial gradient while preserving structural integrity. Through experiments and finite element simulations, the compression–torsion coupling behaviour is systematically investigated, revealing two deformation mechanisms, namely twist-locking and twist-release, and defining the compression–torsion coupling threshold (CTCT). In the twist-locking region, the graded twist enhances spatial constraints and optimises load transfer paths, transforming the deformation from layer-by-layer instability into globally coordinated deformation, thereby synchronously improving the stiffness, plateau stress, and specific energy absorption. Beyond the CTCT, the structure enters the twist-release region, where in-plane rotational degrees of freedom are activated, leading to a degradation of the mechanical properties. The CTCT of the Primitive structure is approximately 60°, whereas for the Gyroid structure, due to differences in surface connectivity, the effective CTCT is lower and the strengthening window is narrower. These mechanisms endow graded-twist TPMS structures with programmable mechanical responses based on geometric parameters, offering new strategies for multifunctional and intelligent structural design.

papers.title: Association of Single-Dose Intravenous Vitamin C with Inpatient Hydromorphone Use After Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Background Postoperative pain control after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) and total hip arthroplasty (THA) commonly includes opioids, which are associated with adverse effects. Vitamin C is reported to reduce postoperative opioid requirements in several surgical settings. Objective To determine whether a single postoperative vitamin C dose added to an established pain management protocol was associated with reduced inpatient hydromorphone use following THA/TKA. Methods Charts of patients who underwent primary TKA (n=100) or THA (n=69) by a single surgeon were retrospectively reviewed. In March 2025, a single 5g intravenous vitamin C dose was incorporated into the postoperative multimodal analgesia protocol. Patients prior to March 2025 were controls (n=122); patients after vitamin C introduction were intervention cohort (n=47). Analgesics and antiemetics were recorded for postoperative day (POD) 0, 1, and 2. Results TKA patients required significantly less hydromorphone than THA patients on POD0 (control: p=0.001; vitamin C: p=0.003). TKA patients in both cohorts had similar total daily hydromorphone use on POD0 and POD2. On POD1, control TKA patients required more hydromorphone (6.1±3.2 mg) than vitamin C TKA patients (4.4±3.0 mg, p=0.036). THA patients in both cohorts had similar total daily hydromorphone use on POD0, 1, and 2. In a linear mixed-effects model, vitamin C administration was associated with reduced hydromorphone/hour of hospital stay (beta coefficient -0.0159, p=0.003). Conclusion A single postoperative 5g intravenous vitamin C dose was associated with reduced inpatient hydromorphone consumption following TKA. Prospective randomized studies are warranted to confirm this association and define the optimal perioperative vitamin C protocol. Level of Evidence III (retrospective cohort study)

papers.title: CEFAZOLIN VERSUS CEFAZOLIN PLUS VANCOMYCIN PROPHYLAXIS FOR PRIMARY THA PATIENTS WITHOUT DOCUMENTED MRSA COLONIZATION: AN ASAP TRIAL-INFORMED PROPENSITY-MATCHED ANALYSIS
papers.abstract: Background Whether vancomycin should be routinely added to cefazolin for perioperative prophylaxis in primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) remains uncertain. The ASAP randomized trial of 1,850 THA patients reported no clear benefit to adding vancomycin to cefazolin in arthroplasty patients without known MRSA colonization, with numerically higher surgical site infection rates in the dual-prophylaxis arm. However, hip-specific estimates were limited by sample size. We evaluated whether similar infection-related patterns were observable in a large U.S. real-world THA cohort. Methods A retrospective propensity-score-matched cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX U.S. Collaborative Network. Adults ≥18 years undergoing primary THA who received day-of-surgery cefazolin plus vancomycin were compared with those who received cefazolin alone. To approximate ASAP eligibility, we excluded patients with prior periprosthetic joint infection, any infection within 30 days pre-operatively, and any documented or suspected MRSA carriage, pre-operative mupirocin use, or pre-operative S. aureus nucleic acid testing. Patients receiving clindamycin, daptomycin, or gentamicin were excluded. Cohorts were 1:1 propensity-score matched on age, sex, race, ethnicity, BMI, comorbidities, and antibiotic allergy status. Outcomes within 90 days included periprosthetic joint infection, surgical site infection (any, superficial, deep), sepsis, lower-limb cellulitis, acute kidney injury, all-cause readmission, and emergency department visits. Results After matching, 88,310 patients (44,155 per arm) were analyzed. The cefazolin plus vancomycin group had a higher coded incidence of 90-day peri-prosthetic joint infection (0.93% vs 0.72%; RR 1.29; p < 0.001), any surgical site infection (0.95% vs 0.75%; RR 1.26; p = 0.001), superficial SSI (RR 1.63; p < 0.001), deep SSI (RR 2.03; p < 0.001), sepsis (RR 1.27; p = 0.009), and 90-day readmission (16.1% vs 12.4%; RR 1.30; p < 0.001). Lower limb cellulitis, acute kidney injury, and emergency department visits did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusion In this large propensity-matched analysis of primary THA patients without documented MRSA colonization, cefazolin plus vancomycin was not associated with lower 90-day infection-related risk compared with cefazolin alone. Instead, dual prophylaxis was associated with higher coded rates of PJI, SSI, sepsis, and readmission. Viewed alongside the ASAP trial, these findings do not provide supportive evidence for routine dual prophylaxis in MRSA-unknown primary THA patients and reinforce the need for more selective, risk-based use of vancomycin. These findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating given the limitations of federated EHR data, including residual confounding by indication, incomplete capture of MRSA screening, inability to verify antibiotic timing, dosing, and reliance on administrative codes.

papers.title: The Role of Bone Grafts in the Management of Complex Fractures
papers.abstract: Complex fractures, which are characterized by substantial loss of bone, severe disintegration, or nonunion, pose significant challenges in the field of orthopedic surgery. Bone grafting is recognized as a valuable technique for enhancing bone healing, restoring structural integrity, and improving functional recovery. Bone grafts are grouped into three types: autografts, allografts, and synthetic substitutes, each with unique benefits and drawbacks. Autografts, which originate from the patient’s own body, have superior osteogenic, osteoinductive, and osteoconductive characteristics, making them the gold standard. Still, donor-site morbidity and limitations on accessibility are concerns. Allografts derived from cadaveric sources offer a possibility that eliminates donor-site complications; however, they are associated with immunological rejection and disease transmission. Synthetic grafts and bioengineered scaffolds are gaining popularity due to their biocompatibility and ability to be customized to individual patient needs, which often incorporate growth factors (e.g., BMPs and VEGF) and stem cells to promote regeneration. The integration of bone grafts with modern surgical procedures, including 3D printing, tissue engineering, and growth factor therapies, has revolutionized the management of fractures. Based on the literature reviewed, 3D-printed scaffolds can offer patient-specific architectures along with controlled mechanical and biological properties, whereas newly developed bioprinting and artificial intelligence-based technologies may enhance scaffold design, vascularization, and regenerative performance. Despite these advances, optimizing graft selection and vascularization remains crucial to achieving optimal outcomes. This review focuses on the role of bone grafts in complex fracture care, specifically their biological and mechanical contributions to bone regeneration. Future research should focus on enhancing scaffold vascularization, biomaterial performance, personalized care, and manufacturing consistency, along with adequately powered preclinical and long-term clinical studies. An interdisciplinary approach involving regenerative medicine, biomechanics, 3D bioprinting, and artificial intelligence may be required to generate more effective and patient-specific treatments for complex bone defects.

papers.title: Numerical and Machine Learning Prediction of Blast and Fragment Propagation in RC Frames Under Internal Explosion
papers.abstract: Each component of reinforced concrete (RC) frames absorbs and dissipates blast energy, mitigating damage to adjacent rooms. Finite element modeling and machine learning are combined to analyze the propagation of blast waves and wall fragments in RC frames. A validated model simulates explosion scenarios with five TNT equivalents and examines blast loading and dynamic responses of adjacent rooms. Orthogonal experimental design is adopted to analyze the attenuation effects of structural parameters (room dimensions, venting coefficient, wall strength and thickness), TNT equivalent, and the number of propagation rooms on power parameters propagated to adjacent rooms. The results reveal that the peak overpressure and impulse of the adjacent rooms decrease by approximately two and one orders of magnitude, respectively, compared with the preceding room. The ejection velocity of wall fragments decays exponentially with the number of propagation rooms, which is the primary factor attenuating the power parameters, followed by the masonry wall strength and thickness. A backpropagation neural network-based surrogate model is developed to predict the attenuation coefficients of the power parameters (peak overpressure, duration, and wall fragment ejection velocity), achieving prediction errors below 20%. The proposed prediction framework provides a computationally efficient alternative to full-scale numerical simulation for rapid damage assessment.

papers.title: Sandwich liner fracture after 21 years from revision total hip arthroplasty: a case report
papers.abstract: Introduction Ceramic-polyethylene sandwich liners were introduced to reduce fracture, but high failure rates were reported. We report a fracture clinically recognized 21 years after revision total hip arthroplasty (THA). Case Presentation A 64-year-old man presented with two weeks of hip pain, clicking, and gait disturbance without trauma. He underwent primary THA for secondary coxarthrosis after slipped capital femoral epiphysis and revision THA for aseptic loosening three years later. Radiographs demonstrated eccentric femoral-head migration and radiopaque fragments. Computed tomography confirmed ceramic layer fracture and migration into the obturator internus muscle. Management and Outcomes Re-revision of the acetabular cup with a fourth-generation ceramic articulation was performed, with the well-fixed femoral stem retained. At 43 months, he returned to recreational hiking; the modified Harris Hip Score improved from 42.9 to 87.5. Residual fragments remained stable. Conclusion Long-term surveillance and prompt evaluation of mechanical symptoms are advised for older-generation sandwich liners.

papers.title: SONICATION BRUSHING EFFECTIVELY REMOVES GRAM-NEGATIVE BIOFILM FROM TIBIAL BASEPLATES: AN IN VITRO STUDY
papers.abstract: Aim Debridement, antibiotics and implant retention (DAIR) is the treatment of choice in acute periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), and residual biofilm on the retained components is likely after debridement. Chemical debridement has been studied rigorously, mechanical methods far less. Dental literature indicates that sonication brushing removes biofilm effectively, but its role in PJI remains largely unexplored. Gram-negative organisms cause 10 to 20% of PJI, E. coli being the most common among them, and they are isolated most often within the first year after arthroplasty, the window in which DAIR is used. DAIR performs worse in gram-negative infection. The purpose of this study was to determine whether sonication brushing removes E. coli biofilm from a tibial baseplate, alone and combined with pulsatile lavage. Methods Five size-D Ti-6Al-4V tibial baseplates were inoculated with E. coli (ATCC 25922) in lysogeny broth and incubated at 37 °C for 72 hours under static conditions. Treatment episodes were allocated to four groups: untreated control (n = 12), high-speed pulsatile lavage (n = 8), sonication brushing (n = 8), or sonication brushing followed by pulsatile lavage (n = 8). Baseplates were reused across runs and rotated between conditions. The primary outcome was viable bacteria (CFU/mL) recovered by bath sonication and serial dilution plating. The secondary outcome was residual biomass by crystal violet staining. CFU data were compared by one-way ANOVA on log10-transformed values with post-hoc Tukey correction. Crystal violet results are descriptive. Results Untreated baseplates yielded a mean of 2.48 × 106 CFU/mL. Pulsatile lavage alone reduced viable bacteria by 32.7% (1.67 × 106 CFU/mL; p = 0.40 vs. control). Sonication brushing achieved an 80.3% reduction (4.90 × 105 CFU/mL; p < 0.001), and the combination a 99.4% reduction (1.48 × 104 CFU/mL; p < 0.001). Every treated baseplate still yielded culturable bacteria. Crystal violet absorbance fell stepwise across treatment groups (30.8%, 36.1%, 44.5%), proportionally less than viable counts. Conclusions Sonication brushing effectively removed E. coli biofilm from titanium tibial baseplates, where pulsatile lavage alone did not. Combining brushing with lavage reduced the bacterial load the most. Viable bacteria remained after every treatment, so chemical decontamination of the retained implant stays important alongside mechanical debridement.

papers.title: Heat Treatment Effect on Corrosion Resistance and Microstructure of Selective Laser Melted 316L Stainless Steel
papers.abstract: Recently, 316L stainless steel fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM) has been widely used in various fields; however, the influence of post-processing heat treatments on its corrosion resistance has not yet been fully clarified in the literature. In this study, the corrosion behavior of SLM-built 316L stainless steel is investigated in its as-built state and after various heat-treatments, and the results are compared with those of conventionally processed (wrought) 316L. Electrochemical measurements show that the SLM-manufactured specimens exhibit lower corrosion resistance than their wrought counterparts. Furthermore, neither stress-relief annealing at 650 °C nor solution (recrystallization) treatment at 1050 °C leads to a measurable improvement in the corrosion resistance of the SLM-manufactured material under the conditions investigated.

papers.title: MICROBIOLOGY OF PERIPROSTHETIC JOINT INFECTION IN TOTAL HIP ARTHROPLASTY: IS ORGANISM PROFILE CHANGING ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND EUROPE?
papers.abstract: Introduction & Aim Regional differences in microbiology and antibiotic resistance in periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) may influence treatment, but direct comparisons of causative organisms between the United States (US) and Europe are limited. This study aimed to evaluate patients undergoing revision total hip arthroplasty (THA) for PJI in order to compare causative organism distribution and antibiotic resistance patterns as well as to evaluate any temporal trends (from 2013-2025) in organism profile between sites in the United States and Europe. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 1,535 patients from 6 distinct high volume PJI referral centers, 4 of which were in the US (n = 824) and 2 of which were in Europe (n = 711). Baseline characteristics, intraoperative culture results, and antibiotic resistance patterns were collected. Patients were grouped by region (US vs Europe) for comparison. The US cohort was younger (median: 65 vs 71 years, p<0.001), had higher body mass index (BMI) (median: 30.2 vs 27.5 kg/m2, p<0.001), and higher Charlson comorbidity index (CCI) (median: 4.0 vs 2.8, p<0.001). Results Organism distribution differed significantly between regions. The US had higher rates of culture negative (47% vs. 10%, p<0.001) and Staphylococcus aureus (15% vs. 8%, p<0.001) infections compared to Europe. Europe had higher rates of coagulase-negative Staphylococcus infections (46% vs. 9%, p<0.001) compared to the US. Europe also had a higher incidence of polymicrobial infection (15% vs. 10%, p<0.001) and anaerobic infections (9% vs. 3%, p<0.001). In contrast, Streptococcus infections were more frequent in the US (6% vs. 3%, p=0.030). Gram-negative (6% vs. 5%, p=0.393), fungal (1% vs. 1%, p=0.525), Enterococcus (2% vs. 1%, p=0.382), mycobacterial (0% vs. 0%, p=0.502), and other organisms (1% vs. 1%, p=0.978) did not differ significantly between regions. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus was more common in the US (5% vs. 1%, p<0.001), while methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative Staphylococcus did not differ between regions (3% vs. 3%, p=0.907). Temporal trends of Staphylococcus aureus isolates remained stable over time in both regions (US: r=0.113, p=0.726; Europe: r=−0.224, p=0.463). In contrast, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcal isolates significantly declined over time, in Europe (r=−0.751, p=0.003) but not in the US (r=−0.490, p=0.106). Conclusions Organism profiles of PJI after THA demonstrate clear geographic variation. In our study there was a higher methicillin-resistance and culture negative incidence in the US, versus more frequent polymicrobial and coagulase-negative infections in Europe. Despite microbiology not changing significantly over time, the distinct profiles between regions reinforces the need for tailored diagnostic, surgical and antibiotic strategies.

papers.title: RATES OF PERIPROSTHETIC JOINT INFECTION FOLLOWING ASEPTIC REVISION TOTAL HIP ARTHROPLASTY ARE NOT REDUCED WITH EXTENDED ORAL ANTIBIOTIC PROPHYLAXIS
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION & AIMS Use of extended oral antibiotic prophylaxis (EOAP) following total hip arthroplasty (THA) has increased despite mixed evidence and no national guidelines. Since revision THA (rTHA) carries increased periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) risk, EOAP use in this setting is particularly relevant. We evaluated postoperative infectious outcomes following rTHA with and without EOAP. METHODS Patients undergoing initial aseptic rTHA were identified in the 2010-2023 Q1 PearlDiver database. Those who received EOAP, defined as postoperative oral antibiotic use >1 day and <2 weeks, were identified. To avoid antibiotic prescriptions for other indications, patients with non-hip infections during the first postoperative week were excluded. EOAP patients were matched 1:4 to controls based on age, sex, and Elixhauser Comorbidity Index (ECI). Median follow-up was 3.74 years in the EOA cohort, and 5.66 years in the no-EOA cohort. Other comorbidities controlled for as covariates included: smoking, BMI≥35kg/m2, chronic kidney disease, autoimmune conditions, and diabetes. The primary endpoint was PJI, with time-to-event analysis performed using Cox regression. Outcomes were assessed at sequential intervals through five-years. Rates of other postoperative infections, emergency department visits and hospital readmissions occurring between 7-90 days were evaluated using multivariable regression. Significance defined as P<0.05. RESULTS After matching, 2,195 EOAP patients were compared to 8,745 control patients. EOAP was not associated with reduced hazard of PJI following 90 days (Hazard ratio [HR]=0.95), 6 months (HR=1.01), 1 year (HR=0.98), 2 years (HR=1.02), or 5 years (HR=0.97) postoperatively (all p>0.05). EOAP patients had lower adjusted odds of experiencing a urinary tract infection (UTI, odds ratio [OR]=0.70, p=0.015) and readmission (OR=0.74, p<0.001) between 7-90 days, without increased odds of C. difficile colitis. CONCLUSION EOAP following aseptic rTHA was not associated with reduced risk of PJI over 5 years. Nonetheless, its use correlated with lower odds of UTI and readmission, suggesting possible alternate short-term benefits

papers.title: Enhanced recovery pathways in total hip and knee arthroplasty: impact on length of stay, complications, and long-term patient-reported outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Introduction Total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) are effective, but recovery involves pain and reduced mobility. Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways combine perioperative interventions to accelerate recovery, but evidence versus conventional care is inconsistent. Objective To evaluate ERAS pathways versus conventional perioperative care in adults undergoing elective primary THA or TKA. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to August 2026. Randomized controlled trials and comparative cohort studies comparing a multimodal ERAS pathway (≥3 components) with conventional care were eligible. Four reviewers extracted data independently. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed, and certainty of evidence was rated using GRADE. Results Twenty-six studies were included (sample sizes 24 to 1,540,462). ERAS shortened length of stay (LOS) in nearly every study; the pooled mean difference was −3.61 days (95% confidence interval [CI], −5.22 to −1.99; I²=97.0%). The reduction was significant for TKA (−3.98 days; 95% CI, −7.04 to −0.92) but not for THA. Overall complications showed a non-significant trend favoring ERAS (risk ratio 0.82; 95% CI, 0.65–1.04), driven mainly by minor (Clavien-Dindo grade 1–2) events. Readmissions, transfusion, and opioid requirements did not differ significantly. Conclusion ERAS pathways are associated with a clinically important reduction in LOS, particularly for TKA. A reduction in perioperative morbidity is plausible but unconfirmed. Evidence on readmissions, opioid use, and long-term patient-reported outcomes is limited and of low certainty. Well-designed multicenter randomized trials with standardized long-term outcome reporting are needed.

papers.title: Primary or staged re-implantation with no exposures for orbital implants requiring explantation: a retrospective study over 10 years
papers.abstract: Orbital implant exposure is a frequent and challenging complication following eye removal. Large exposures or infected defects often require implant removal, leading to complex challenges in volume restoration. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and surgical outcomes of managing orbital implant exposure requiring explantation followed by a specific protocol of one-stage replacement or secondary implantation. This retrospective study included 43 patients who underwent orbital implant removal between January 2012 and December 2023. Patients were categorized into non-infection ( n = 11) and infection ( n = 32) groups. The non-infected group received one-stage implant replacement, while the infection group underwent a staged approach: initial explantation and infection control, followed by delayed secondary implantation at least 3 months later. Clinical characteristics, re-exposure rate, and long-term surgical outcomes were analyzed. Late exposure (> 3 months post-implantation) occurred in 90.7% of cases, with a mean interval of 62.1 ± 63.1 months. The infection group exhibited a significantly longer clinical course from symptom onset to explantation compared to the non-infection group (27.2 ± 29.3 vs. 9.4 ± 7.1 months, P = 0.0089). Eye-socket contracture was observed in 28 patients (65.1%), with a higher incidence trend observed in infected cases (71.88% vs. 45.45%). Among the 26 patients who received a new porous polyethylene implant, none experienced recurrent exposure, extrusion, or pyogenic granuloma over a mean follow-up of 64.4 months. Five patients (19.2%) reported postoperative volume deficiency. Tailoring surgical management to the infection status provides excellent long-term outcomes for patients requiring orbital implant explantation. Immediate primary replacement is safe for non-infected cases, whereas a staged secondary implantation strategy with meticulous surgical techniques is highly effective for infected cases to prevent re-exposure. Given that prolonged infection exacerbate socket contracture, early clinical recognition and prompt surgical intervention are paramount.

papers.title: Coupled effects of topology and Al content on microstructure and mechanical behavior of LPBF-fabricated FeCoNiCrTi0.2Alx porous HEAs via multiscale studies
papers.abstract: This study, by combining molecular dynamics simulations, finite element simulations, and laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) experiments, systematically reveals the coupled regulation mechanism of four topological structures (tetrahedral, diamond, octahedral, and dodecahedral) and Al content (x = 0–0.3) on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and fracture behavior of FeCoNiCrTi 0.2 Al x porous high-entropy alloy (HEA). LAMMPS simulations show that the plastic deformation of the alloy is jointly mediated by the slip of 1/6 < 112 > Shockley partial dislocations and the FCC-to-HCP phase transformation. The strength reaches its peak value when the Al content is 0.3, and Al achieves significant strengthening by increasing lattice distortion and reducing stacking fault energy. DEFORM simulations and experiments confirm that the compressive response of porous structures is highly dependent on the topological configuration. Due to the supporting effect of horizontal struts, the tetrahedral structure exhibits the highest compressive strength (reaching 905.54 MPa for FeCoNiCrTi 0.2 Al 0.3 ) and elastic modulus (5019.94 MPa), but a relatively short plastic plateau stage. The diamond structure exhibits the optimal energy absorption capacity (reaching 198.12 MJ/m 3 ) and the longest densification strain (~ 53%) due to the progressive bending of inclined struts. The octahedral and dodecahedral structures show intermediate performance. This study provides a theoretical basis and experimental support for the design and application of lightweight porous HEAs.

papers.title: Cryotherapy Following Nonknee Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: What Is the Issue? Joint replacement surgeries remain among the highest-volume inpatient procedures in Canada. This major operation replaces a damaged joint with an artificial implant to relieve severe pain and restore mobility. While joint replacement can significantly improve a patient's quality of life, the recovery phase involves acute pain and swelling at the surgical site that requires postoperative care to improve recovery. Cold therapies, such as ice packs, are part of the standard postoperative care and recovery to reduce swelling, inflammation, and pain. Cryotherapy devices are specialized interventions for cold therapy that are designed to offer lower and/or more consistent temperatures than conventional ice packs. However, the clinical effectiveness of cryotherapy after surgical replacement of joints other than the knee is unclear. This rapid review was prepared in response to a request for evidence to support decision-making around the use of cryotherapy after nonknee arthroplasty. What Did We Do? Canada’s Drug Agency conducted a rapid review to identify and summarize evidence that evaluated the clinical effectiveness of cryotherapy compared with standard postoperative care in adult patients undergoing nonknee arthroplasty. We searched key resources, including journal citation databases, and conducted a focused internet search for relevant evidence published between January 1, 2023, and August 11, 2026. What Did We Find? We found 1 systematic review that evaluated cryotherapy postoperatively in adult patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty and 1 nonrandomized clinical trial that evaluated cryotherapy following carpometacarpal arthroplasty. We did not find studies on the clinical effectiveness of cryotherapy versus standard of care for shoulder, elbow, wrist, or ankle joint arthroplasties. Compared with standard of care, cryotherapy may be associated with improved pain during the first 2 postoperative days following total hip arthroplasty and 2 weeks after carpometacarpal arthroplasty without increasing the risk of adverse events. The included studies did not detect statistically significant differences between cryotherapy and control groups for analgesic use, blood loss, joint function, adverse events, or hospital length of stay. The clinical evidence summarized in this rapid review is of low to moderate quality, with substantial concerns regarding selection bias, lack of randomization, intervention masking, and generalizability. What Does This Mean? Health care professionals and decision-makers can use this evidence to inform decisions around the use of cryotherapy after hip and carpometacarpal joint replacements. Low-certainty evidence suggests that cryotherapy might offer short-term pain relief, but patients might not experience benefits in other clinical outcomes. Well-designed studies with proper reporting are needed to confirm the clinical effectiveness of cryotherapy versus other cold therapies.

papers.title: POLYHEXANIDE COMBINED WITH MECHANICAL OR ULTRASONIC DISRUPTION ENABLES RAPID ERADICATION OF IMPLANT-ASSOCIATED BIOFILMS
papers.abstract: Background Successful debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) requires near-complete removal of biofilm from retained implant components to prevent bacterial persistence and infection recurrence. This study evaluated polyhexanide (PHMB) alone and in combination with mechanical and ultrasonic disruption for implant-associated biofilms. Materials and Methods Immature biofilms of Staphylococcus epidermidis (ATCC 35984) and Escherichia coli (ATCC 25922) were grown on Ti-6Al-4V, CoCrMo, and polyethylene (PE) discs. PHMB concentration screening (0.0004–0.04%) identified sub-eradicative but strongly inhibitory conditions for combination testing. In the main experiments, PHMB was applied at species- and material-specific concentrations (0.004% on metals; 0.04% on PE for S. epidermidis; 0.004% for E. coli). Biofilms were exposed for 1 minute to PHMB alone or combined with sonication, mechanical toothbrushing, or ultrasonic toothbrushing. Biofilm removal was quantified by CFU from detached fractions, and residual metabolic activity was assessed by isothermal microcalorimetry (IMC). Results PHMB at 0.02–0.04% suppressed metabolic activity of both species on Ti-6Al-4V and CoCrMo, and of E. coli on PE, while S. epidermidis on PE showed only partial suppression, guiding concentration selection for main experiments. All single-modality treatments reduced biofilm metabolic activity but did not achieve complete suppression. No CFU were recovered from PHMB-treated samples, likely due to carryover during sampling of the detached fraction. In contrast, PHMB combined with sonication, mechanical brushing, or ultrasonic brushing achieved complete suppression of biofilm metabolic activity across all materials and both species within 1 minute. Conclusion PHMB combined with mechanical or ultrasonic disruption enables rapid and complete eradication of implant-associated biofilms. Among the evaluated approaches, the ultrasonic brushing system represents a readily translatable, clinically applicable device for intraoperative biofilm management. This strategy achieves consistent biofilm eradication within one minute across materials and bacterial species, supporting its potential role in DAIR procedures.

papers.title: Reassessing AC/DC Selectivity and Efficiency in Sequential Electroreductions
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper reassesses the selectivity, efficiency, and mechanism of sequential electroreductions of carbonyl compounds under alternating current (AC) versus direct current (DC) conditions. It reflects the constructive dialogue─through multiple rounds of revisions of the present work─between the Baran group (authors of the original report) and the Grzybowski group (who sought to reproduce the reported phenomena and develop theoretical models). Ultimately, consensus was reached that under the originally described conditions, AC offers no systematic yield or selectivity advantage over DC; side reactions are outcompeted by mass action rather than kinetically suppressed by AC waveforms, while DC is faster and more energy efficient (less F mol–1). Higher AC yields and selectivities can be reached when a small amount of base is added to the sacrificial pivalic acid reductant. This improvement, documented in Baran’s Corrigendum, was confirmed in our own reproductions. However, the addition of base fundamentally alters the originally proposed mechanism: the observed behavior can no longer be attributed to frequency or waveform effects imparted by AC forcing, but is instead explained by mass-action considerations and pH conditions at the electrodes. Moreover, with base present, AC yields and selectivities can still be matched or even surpassed under appropriately optimized DC conditions. These findings (i) clarify the mechanistic origins of the reported phenomena, (ii) establish a transparent framework for choosing between AC and DC electrolysis in future synthetic applications, and (iii) showcase the value of using Machine Learning techniques (here reaction selection aided by Bayesian Optimization) in optimizing electrochemical processes.

papers.title: Resolving phonons in superconductor Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ at sub-unit-cell resolution
papers.abstract: Abstract The role of phonons in cuprates remains controversial, with their complex lattice structure complicating the investigation. Here, we identify phonon modes originating from charge reservoir and superconducting layers of Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ using sub-unit-cell resolved electron energy loss spectroscopy in a scanning transmission electron microscope. We reveal several phonon modes exhibiting layer-specific localization: ~78 meV in-plane modes localized in the CuO 2 planes, ~42 meV hybrid (in-plane and out-of-plane) modes in the CuO 2 planes, and ~38 meV hybrid modes in the BiO layers. We also observe a periodic modulation of phonon frequencies induced by the superstructure, spatially correlating with the superconducting gap variation. Our findings offer new insights into the lattice dynamics in cuprates, fostering deeper exploration of the microscopic linkage between structural modulation, electronic inhomogeneity, and electron-phonon coupling.

papers.title: regTPS: a novel approach to approximate a Gaussian random field for Bayesian spatial modeling
papers.abstract: Abstract Gaussian random field is a ubiquitous model for spatial phenomena in diverse scientific disciplines. Its approximation is often crucial for computational feasibility in simulation, inference, and uncertainty quantification. The Karhunen–Loéve Expansion provides an optimal low-rank representation of a (spatial) stochastic process, but its practical implementation relies heavily on how the underlying covariance structure is specified. In this work, we propose a novel approach called regTPS, which constructs a spatial covariance by formulating the inverse of a regularized thin plate spline operator. By computing the eigendecomposition of the regularized biharmonic operator, regTPS induces a smoothness prior that hierarchically allocates variance across spatial frequencies. We evaluate the statistical performance and computational efficiency of regTPS relative to the established stochastic partial differential equations approach within an MCMC algorithm in two different simulation designs. Across various simulation scenarios, the regTPS method achieved predictive accuracy comparable to the SPDE approach. Moreover, regTPS substantially reduced the effective parameter dimension, with reductions of approximately 43–52% for large sample sizes. Also, within a mesh independent simulation setting, regTPS consistently maintains its predictive accuracy under both Matérn and exponential covariance functions, keeping an optimal balance between basis-dimension reduction and sampling efficiency. Lastly, application to real $$\text {NO}_2$$ NO 2 data concentrations using 10-fold and leave-one-out cross-validation establishes that regTPS obtain a competitive predictive accuracy against SPDE and nearest-neighbor Gaussian process models. Thus, regTPS presents a rigorous, low-dimensional, and computational efficient alternative for Bayesian spatial modeling.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural modeling of TiO2 photoanode thickness-dependent electron transport and photovoltaic performance in dye-sensitized solar cells
papers.abstract: Abstract The thickness of a photoanode in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) simultaneously influences the dye-accessible volume, optical path length, electron-transport distance and recombination. To estimate this competition, a physics-informed neural network was constructed based on the six compressed TiO 2 photoanodes used by Tsai et al. The spatial state is expressed as a random-feature (RF) neural field u θ (x i , d), with normalized depth, x i = x/d, and film thickness, d. The field is bound by a steady-state diffusion-generation-recombination equation, and extraction and zero-flux boundary conditions. In the 6 devices dataset, the contact-gradient current was mapped with a low-capacity regularized thickness correction, using the PDE result as a fixed value (inverse parameters effective electron diffusion coefficient, electron lifetime, effective photon flux and photon flux). The analytic solution of contact current and relative least square (L 2 ) error of 0.997–1.001 and 0.08–0.68% respectively confirmed the neural field. The last device model resulted in training Mean Absolute Percentage Errors (MAPEs) of 7.03% for J SC , 1.00% for V OC , 1.55% for FF, and 6.44% for algebraically consistent efficiency. The efficiency MAPE of leave-one-thickness-out validation outperformed the results of linear regression (27.76%), quadratic regression (26.08%), natural cubic spline interpolation (78.42%), Gaussian-process regression (19.34%), and a conventional ANN (20.15%). The continuous model gave optimum thickness as 29.72 µm at 8.70% efficiency, while jackknife resampling revealed that the thickness has a significant uncertainty, as only six devices exist. A frozen model transfer to an independent published thickness series yielded the MAPE of 17.10%, indicating a low level of cross-system transfer, and a need for morphology and electrolyte-aware inputs. The study thus presents a physics-regularized small data framework that discriminates between within-system predictive value and universal DSSC generalization, which can be replicated.

papers.title: School Accident Education in Reducing Pediatric Trauma Burden: An Examination of Education for Children Aged 6–12
papers.abstract: Aims To evaluate the impact of a nurse-led safety educational intervention on primary school students’ safety knowledge scores and to analyze the epidemiological characteristics and clinical trauma burden of school accidents. Background Primary schools represent a critical setting for non-fatal pediatric mechanical trauma. Children aged 6–12 years experience higher injury rates than younger or older peers, accounting for 10%–20% of pediatric emergency visits and trauma admissions. Pediatric surgical and school nurses play key roles in injury prevention, triage, and trauma management. Introduction School accidents—predominantly falls and collisions—frequently cause extremity fractures, head injuries, and complex soft-tissue lacerations requiring surgical evaluation, debridement, or suturing. Interactive, nurse-led educational programs using active learning techniques enhance danger recognition and serve as cost-effective strategies to mitigate trauma burden. Methods A one-group pretest–posttest quasi-experimental study was conducted with 77 students (aged 8–10 years; 3rd/4th grade) during the 2024–2025 academic year. Trained nursing students delivered interactive safety training under academic oversight. Results Prior to training, 51.9% reported experiencing a school injury, with 40.0% reporting recurrent events. Most injuries occurred during recess (85.0%) on playgrounds (72.5%) via falls (82.5%) and collisions (40.0%), causing mobility restrictions in 42.5% and absenteeism in 45.0% of cases. Safety knowledge scores significantly increased post-intervention from 95.25 ± 9.44 to 119.63 ± 5.37 ( p < .001). Discussion Structured, interactive nurse-led education effectively improves safety knowledge and risk perception among primary school children. High rates of mobility impairment and school absenteeism highlight the substantial trauma burden and emphasize the necessity of proactive nursing interventions. Conclusion/Implications for Nursing and Health Policy Nurse-led educational interventions significantly enhance safety knowledge in primary school children. Given the clinical burden of fractures, lacerations, and missed school days, pediatric surgical and school health nurses must lead injury prevention programs. Integrating nurse-led safety curricula into primary education should be prioritized in public health policies.

papers.title: PINN-based functional inference in size-structured population models: Application to fish oogenesis
papers.abstract: Early oogenesis in juvenile fish establishes the ovarian reserve, which conditions lifelong reproductive capacity. This process is regulated by local hormonal feedback mechanisms, mainly involving Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH). In this work, we develop a mechanistic size-structured population model describing an unstructured germ-cell compartment and a population of growing oocytes, with AMH feedback on the renewal of the precursor cells compartment. Using repeated cross-sectional observations of oocyte size distributions in fish ovaries, we formulate and solve a nonlinear inverse problem with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to infer three demographic functions: the size-dependent oocyte growth rate, the AMH-regulated net renewal rate of the precursor cells compartment, and the recruitment rate of new oocytes. We introduce an auxiliary PINN formulation to handle the nonlocal interaction term and jointly infer unobserved state variables and demographic functions. Our inference strategy combines non-parametric PINNs with a data-guided model-selection step: demographic functions are first inferred without prescribing their functional forms, and the learned profiles are then used to select parsimonious parametric laws, whose parameters are subsequently estimated within a parametric PINN. We investigate identifiability at both the functional and parametric levels, combining structural identifiability analysis with synthetic-data experiments assessing the practical recovery of functions and parameters. The inference procedure is embedded within an individual-level bootstrap framework to assess sensitivity to repeated-cross-sectional sampling and stochastic training. Applied to juvenile fish oogenesis, the framework recovers interpretable growth and renewal dynamics, provides access to unobserved quantities, and enables conditional in silico investigation. More broadly, this work provides a framework for functional and parametric inference in size-structured population models with nonlocal interactions from sparse cross-sectional data.

papers.title: Offset-free 3DOF Ball and Plate Tracking Control Using Velocity-form Integral MPC
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a disturbance-observer-assisted velocity-form integral model predictive control (MPC) structure for reference trajectory tracking on a physical three-degree-of-freedom (3DOF) Ball and Plate system. Under the small-angle assumption, the system dynamics are approximated as decoupled linear subsystems along the x- and y-axes, allowing identical MPC controllers to be applied independently to each axis. Conventional nominal-model-based MPC can exhibit steady-state tracking offsets because of model–plant mismatches, including plate-zero alignment uncertainty, actuator mismatch, sensor noise, velocity estimation errors, and residual cross-axis coupling. To mitigate these effects, a velocity-form integral MPC is formulated using state and input increments, with an augmented state containing an accumulated output term for offset-free tracking. However, direct use of state increments can make the controller sensitive to measurement noise and velocity estimation errors. Therefore, a Luenberger-observer-based disturbance observer reconstructs the system state using the innovation between the nominal model’s one-step prediction and the measured output. The reconstructed state is used to form the observer-based augmented state, improving the reliability of the initial condition for MPC prediction. Experimental results show that the proposed controller achieves stable trajectory tracking on the physical system and reduces steady-state tracking offsets under constant disturbances.

papers.title: Unsupervised Physics-constrained Learning for Upper-limb Joint Angle Estimation From IMU Sensors
papers.abstract: In Learning from demonstration, accurate and continuous capture of human upper-limb motion during actual work is essential for accumulating large-scale robot training data, and can also populate a digital twin with realistic human motion for safe pre-deployment policy validation. However, acquiring such data at scale using optical motion capture is impractical because of its cost and limited capture volume. This paper proposes a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) that estimates shoulder and elbow joint angles using two IMUs attached to the upper arm and forearm, trained solely using physical constraints and no external ground-truth labels. The loss combines a quaternion/angle kinematics residual, a gravity-vector consistency term, an anatomical range-of-motion constraint, and an initial-alignment anchor, requiring no ground-truth trajectory. Training uses unlabeled IMU data; a limited set of encoder-based angle references from a mechanical device is reserved exclusively for evaluation. Experiments using real IMU data show the proposed label-free method outperforms raw gyroscope integration and, on a slow repetitive motion trial, even outperforms a supervised PINN trained with the same encoder labels, while also revealing a gap in generalization when the model is asked to extrapolate beyond its training window.

papers.title: Federated variational inference for incomplete multimodal learning
papers.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) often preceding its onset. Early prediction of MCI progression to AD is crucial for effective intervention. Although multimodal neuroimaging can improve prediction accuracy, incomplete datasets and strict privacy regulations hinder broad implementation in machine learning (ML) models. Current federated learning (FL) solutions in neuroimaging typically focus on unimodal data, thereby missing the synergistic advantages of multimodal approaches. We propose Federated Variational Inference for Cross-Model Learning (FedVICML), a novel FL framework that allows institutions with varying neuroimaging modalities to collaboratively train predictive models without centralized data sharing, thus keeping raw patient data local to each site. FedVICML uniquely combines FL with a new cross-model variational inference (VI) method, using two distinct Bayesian neural networks for multimodal and unimodal data respectively, and an extended VI-based mechanism for knowledge transfer. This decentralized, data-local approach enables robust learning with incomplete multimodal data by integrating FL and cross-model VI, without pooling raw data across sites. We apply FedVICML to simulated and real-world datasets from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), demonstrating improved performance and uncertainty quantification over conventional FL baselines for predicting MCI to AD progression. Our results highlight FedVICML’s promise for collaborative medical research in heterogeneous data environments.

papers.title: Generative AI in Gamified Learning: A Systematic Literature Review on Student Motivation
papers.abstract: This Systematic Literature Review (SLR) synthesizes how Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) is implemented in learning environments, with and without gamification, and what studies report about students’ motivation and engagement. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, structured searches in Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect identified 792 records, and 116 full-text reports were assessed. Sixty-nine peer-reviewed journal articles were included: 21 on AI-supported gamified or game-based learning and 48 on Generative AI and motivation or engagement without gamification. In the gamified subset, four implementation forms appear (AI characters and role-play partners, LLM feedback and adaptive difficulty, AI-generated assessment items, and Generative AI as a game design tool), and all eight comparison studies reported higher or favorable motivation, engagement, or related outcomes. Across the whole corpus, two meta-analyses and one systematic review report positive overall effects of ChatGPT and Generative AI on engagement or motivation, with moderators and mixed emotional evidence. Individual studies are not uniformly positive: one found that videos outperformed a Generative AI assistant on knowledge gains and curiosity, one found no significant effect on behavioral engagement, and one found that Generative AI use may reduce active learning and motivation. The evidence is concentrated in higher education (48 of 69 articles) and in 2025 (52 of 69); the most frequently stated limitations are small or single-context samples (20 articles) and short interventions with novelty effects (12), and the most frequent recommendations are longer studies (18) and larger and more diverse samples (17). Future research should isolate the AI component's contribution and test it over time. Keywords: Generative AI, Gamification, Gamified learning, Student motivation, Systematic review of literature.

papers.title: Scaffolding rubric literacy in international business education: the role of spacing and social sensemaking
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how instructional design can scaffold rubric literacy in international business education. It examines whether pedagogical scaffolds that provide structured time and social space for interpretation can help bridge performance gaps associated with differences in students’ prior academic socialization. Design/methodology/approach A quasi-experimental retrospective design was used to analyze 243 graduate students across eight course sections (2022–2025) at an Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)-accredited university. The design included an explicit no-scaffold comparison condition comprising Sections 3 and 4 (N = 70). The analysis evaluated three instructional configurations: temporal assignment spacing (early rubric release), video explainers and interactive peer-based social sensemaking discussions. Prior rubric exposure was measured at the student level and examined as a moderator of the scaffold–performance relationships. The authors modeled performance alignment using OLS regression with section-clustered robust standard errors. Findings The baseline analysis identifies an initial difference in rubric-aligned performance, with students without prior rubric exposure scoring lower than students with prior exposure. Regression models reveal that instructor-narrated video explainers were not significantly associated with higher rubric-aligned performance. By contrast, both assignment spacing and structured social sensemaking showed positive relationships with rubric-aligned performance. Crucially, the interaction between social sensemaking and prior rubric familiarity was negative and significant, indicating that the positive relationship between sensemaking and rubric-aligned performance was stronger among students without prior rubric exposure, a pattern consistent with an equity-closing role for collaborative interpretation. Originality/value This study moves beyond a technical view of assessment to reframe rubric literacy as a relational, pedagogical capacity co-constructed through active learning design. It contributes to international business education by suggesting that institutional fairness-through-standardization may be contingent on fairness-through-sensemaking, offering clear strategic implications for quality assurance and AACSB assurance of learning processes.

papers.title: Fracture Propagation Simulation and Comprehensive Fracability Evaluation of the Thin Interbedded Tight Sandstone Reservoir: A Case Study of Chunliang Oilfield
papers.abstract: Thin interbedded tight sandstone reservoirs in the Chunliang Oilfield are characterized by strong vertical heterogeneity, pronounced interlayer in situ stress interference, and limited vertical hydraulic fracture propagation, which together make the stimulated reservoir volume (SRV) difficult to predict. To address these challenges, this study integrates core triaxial compression tests, true triaxial hydraulic fracturing experiments, and finite-element numerical simulations. The controlling mechanisms of the horizontal stress difference, the elastic modulus contrast between reservoir and barrier layers, interlayer cementation strength, and fracturing fluid viscosity on fracture propagation are systematically investigated. The results show that when the horizontal stress difference is less than 5 MPa and the elastic modulus contrast between reservoir and barrier layers is less than 10 GPa, hydraulic fractures more readily penetrate the interlayer interface and form complex fracture networks. With increasing stress difference or elastic modulus contrast, fractures tend to propagate as single planar fractures or become constrained by barrier-layer shielding. Strong interlayer cementation suppresses fracture extension and reduces the stimulated area, whereas high fracturing fluid viscosity causes the fracture geometry to transform from a long and narrow pattern to a short and wide pattern. On this basis, a comprehensive fracability evaluation model is established by integrating the brittleness of both reservoir and barrier layers and the stress difference within and between layers. Field applications to 12 representative wells in the Chunliang Oilfield show that the comprehensive fracability index is positively correlated with the stimulated reservoir volume. The proposed model can effectively quantify interlayer stress shielding and provides a basis for fracturing layer selection and parameter optimization in the thin interbedded tight sandstone reservoir.

papers.title: Deep learning and adaptive carrier Phase–Doppler weighted fusion for GNSS cycle slip detection and repair
papers.abstract: Abstract Cycle-slip detection and repair is a critical preprocessing step in high-precision Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning. Under varying cycle-slip ratios, detection thresholds are difficult to determine adaptively, leading to missed detections, false alarms, and suboptimal repair. This paper proposes a deep-learning cycle-slip detection and repair method based on Satellite- and Epoch-Differenced (SDED) observations and develops an adaptive Phase-Doppler (PD) weighted fusion mechanism for kinematic observations. The SDED representation suppresses common-mode errors and highlights cycle-slip signatures. A cycle slip is detected when the prediction residual exceeds the detection threshold, and the rounded residual is used directly as the repair correction. For kinematic observations, PD residuals provide complementary physical consistency information and are adaptively fused with the deep-learning decision through a noise quality factor weighting scheme to suppress false alarms. Bayesian optimization is used to tune the model parameters, and the Transformer, CNN, and LSTM are benchmarked against the Time-Differenced Carrier Phase (TDCP) method across different frequencies, observation modes, and cycle-slip ratios. The Transformer achieves the best overall performance, with detection success rates consistently above 99% and repair success rates above 97% under static conditions, and mean repair errors below 0.11 cycles. Under kinematic conditions, the TF-PD fusion model achieves detection rates above 98.6%, repair rates above 96%, and precision and F1 scores above 94% and 96%, respectively. In real-world PPP experiments, TF-PD reduces the shipborne 3D RMSE by 11.70%, 7.12%, and 6.67% relative to polynomial fitting, PD, and TDCP, respectively, and reduces the vehicular 3D RMSE by 37.30%, 16.15%, and 9.14%, demonstrating enhanced stability and reliability of cycle-slip processing.

papers.title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Degradation-Aware and Coordinated Control of Virtual Power Plants
papers.abstract: Abstract Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) coordinate distributed energy resources (DERs) under forecast uncertainty and multi-time-scale constraints, while battery and generator wear can erase short-term trading gains. This paper proposes a hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) controller that matches aggregator practice: a slow-time-scale manager issues location-level power subgoals together with a continuous autonomy signal, and fast-time-scale workers dispatch devices under local physics. Battery and generator degradation enter the training reward through a three-phase curriculum that activates a throughput-budget penalty and a cycle-depth surcharge, so the policy optimizes profit net of wear rather than arbitrage alone. On a 100-day shared-seed benchmark against two decentralized RL controllers, an open-loop stochastic mixed-integer programming (MIP) day-ahead optimizer, and a closed-loop model predictive control (MPC) baseline that reoptimizes hourly over an 8-h horizon, HRL attains an average daily profit of \$50,264─3.1× MPC and 4.0× MIP─at 50–170 ms per simulated day. HRL is the only method whose throughput-to-cycle-depth ratio exceeds unity (1.18), and it incurs only \$24.6 of cycle-depth-aware wear per \$1,000 of profit (2.5× better than MPC). These results indicate that degradation-aware hierarchical control can outperform both open-loop stochastic optimization and receding-horizon MPC for real-time VPP dispatch.
