papers.title: BUG, DRUG, TIMING: HOW A REAL-WORLD MULTIDISCIPLINARY FRAMEWORK OPTIMISES ANTIMICROBIAL STEWARDSHIP IN HIP AND KNEE PERIPROSTHETIC JOINT INFECTION
papers.abstract: Introduction and aim Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains a challenging complication of hip and knee arthroplasty, with European one-year incidence estimated at 0.5–1.2% for total hip arthroplasty (THA) and ~1–2% for total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Outcomes depend on timely diagnosis, appropriate microbiological sampling, and optimised antimicrobial therapy, increasingly managed by a multidisciplinary team (MDT). This study evaluated real-world antimicrobial stewardship practices, adherence to guideline-based principles, and their association with clinical outcomes within a structured MDT model. Methods Retrospective single-centre study in a Portuguese secondary care hospital. All hip and knee PJI discussed at a MDT meeting (Orthopaedics, Infectious Diseases, Clinical Microbiology and Pharmacy) over two years (2024–2025) were analysed. Results Eighty-five patients were discussed and all but one met EBJIS criteria for confirmed or likely PJI. The cohort was 53% male, median age of 76 years, high comorbidity burden (median five chronic conditions), and functional status impairment in 29%. THA accounted for 66% of discussed cases. Early-onset PJI incidence was 1.7% for THA and 0.8% for TKA. Globally, primary arthroplasties comprised 60% of infections. A total of 124 isolates were identified from deep-tissue sampling (median of seven intraoperative samples per patient), with coagulase-negative staphylococci predominating (58/124). Infections were monomicrobial in 54%, polymicrobial in 38% and culture-negative in 8% (two later yielded Candida spp. on repeat sampling). Multidrug-resistant organisms (MRO) were identified in 13 cases. Empirical antimicrobial therapy was dual in 87% of cases, most commonly piperacillin/tazobactam+vancomycin (65/74), with a median duration of seven days (range 0–46). Targeted therapy almost exclusively involved spectrum narrowing, typically to vancomycin-based regimens (monotherapy in 13 cases and combination therapy in four polymicrobial infections). Two MRO cases required escalation. Early oral switch during this initial phase was uncommon (8%) and median intravenous duration was 14 days. Most cases were managed with debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR; 66%), achieving 80% success. Overall treatment failure (defined as persistent infection, the need for suppressive antibiotic therapy, or prosthesis removal) occurred in 25%, with surgical revision in 15%. Mortality was 6% at 30 days and 9% at one year. Conclusions MDT-driven management achieved favourable outcomes, with low TKA PJI incidence and DAIR success exceeding published pooled estimates (~64%). Extensive intraoperative sampling may have contributed to the low culture-negative rate. Higher early mortality likely reflects comorbidity burden. Prolonged intravenous therapy and limited early oral transition highlight opportunities to optimise stewardship, consistent with OVIVA and DATIPO recommendations.

papers.title: Multi-Response Process-Thickness-Property Optimization of Thin-Walled AlSi10Mg Alloy Fabricated by Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) of AlSi10Mg alloy is highly sensitive to processing conditions, particularly when thin-walled components are fabricated. This study investigates the combined effects of wall thickness, laser power, scan speed, and hatch distance on the mechanical performance of LPBF-fabricated AlSi10Mg. A Box–Behnken design (BBD) based on response surface methodology was employed using 27 experimental runs. Wall thickness was varied from 1 to 3 mm, laser power from 320 to 380 W, scan speed from 730 to 1070 mm/s, and hatch distance from 80 to 130 μm. Relative density (RD), ultimate tensile strength (UTS), yield strength (YS), elongation at fracture, and hardness were evaluated as response variables. The statistical analysis showed that wall thickness and scan speed were the most influential factors for tensile properties, whereas the effects on RD, elongation, and hardness involved additional interaction and nonlinear terms. Among the developed models, the predictive performance is quite adequate along with comparatively higher fitted R2 values; however, only the RDrelative density model performance is limited by giving a negative predicted R2. Optimization of the four mechanical responses, excluding relative density, identified an exploratory candidate at 3.0 mm wall thickness, 320 W laser power, 1070 mm/s scan speed, and approximately 100.46 μm hatch distance. The corresponding predicted UTS, YS, elongation, and hardness were 354.7 MPa, 193.8 MPa, 13.54%, and 112.6 HV, respectively, with a composite desirability of 0.892. The results demonstrate the importance of considering component wall thickness together with LPBF process parameters when optimizing the overall mechanical performance of thin-walled AlSi10Mg components.

papers.title: Enhanced thermoelectric power factor of graphene-Ba-Co-O composites via interfacial charge transport
papers.abstract: Cobalt oxide based thermoelectric have attracted attention due to their high thermal stability and relatively large thermopower at room temperature. However their practical applications are limited by low electrical conductivity, which hindered the thermoelectrical power factor. In present study, the structural and thermoelectric properties of cobalt oxide-based materials systematically investigated through compositional tuning and graphene incorporation. Initially, Na-Co-O compound with different sodium content were synthesized to examine the influence of cation stoichiometry on structural and transport properties. To further modify lattice structure, alkaline earth elements (Ca, Sr and Ba) were introduced into cobalt oxide and structural analysis suggesting that lattice distortion due to the difference in ionic radii. Among all, Ba-based cobalt oxide composition exhibits relatively higher electrical conductivity by maintain thermopower. To overcome intrinsic electrical conductivity, graphene has been added into the Ba 0.33 CoO 2 . These composite exhibited enhancement of thermoelectric power factor of 894 µW/mK 2 at room temperature. This enhancement is attributed to the formation of graphene conductive network and additional phonon scattering sites within the composites, which may help to break the interrelation between thermopower and electrical conductivity. These results highlighting the effectiveness of interfacial transport engineering in cobalt oxide thermoelectric materials.

papers.title: Trajectory Tracking Control for Autonomous Vehicles based on Gaussian Process Regression and Adaptive Control Increment Constraint Adjustment
papers.abstract: Under high-speed and extreme conditions, model mismatch of autonomous vehicles leads to degraded tracking accuracy and reduced lateral stability performance. To solve this problem, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) method using Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) is proposed in this paper. Based on this, an adaptive strategy for adjusting control increment constraints based on steering angle variation is developed using the prediction variance of GPR. This method employs GPR to learn the single-step residuals between the nominal 3-Degree-of-Freedom (3-DOF) vehicle model and its high-fidelity counterpart in Carsim, and then compensates for these residuals recursively within the MPC prediction horizon. Meanwhile, this method uses the prediction variance of GPR as the uncertainty indicator of the GPR model, and establishes an adaptive mapping relationship between the uncertainty parameters and the control increment constraints. When the uncertainty of the GPR model is high, the system actively reduces the control increment constraint. On the Carsim/Simulink platform, the proposed framework is validated under double lane change maneuvers. Simulation results show that, for high-speed dry-road scenarios, the GPR-MPC method lowers the lateral error peak by 16.2% and the heading error peak by 12.7%, compared to the baseline MPC. The A-GPR-MPC method with an adaptive control increment constraint adjustment strategy can, while maintaining the tracking accuracy, further reduce the peak yaw rate by 9.2% and the peak sideslip angle by 8.4%. Under the medium-speed wet road conditions, the A-GPR-MPC can further reduce the peak yaw rate by 9.0%, the peak sideslip angle by 19.0%, and the peak front wheel steering angle by 24.1%. These results demonstrate the proposed method's ability to enhance both tracking accuracy and lateral stability.

papers.title: Choreographing CAV Formations on the Fly with Reflection
papers.abstract: Abstract Formation control of connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) has shown great potential for improving traffic efficiency and safety. However, most existing studies focus on tracking predefined formations for fixed tasks, offering limited adaptability to changing task requirements. To address this limitation, we propose GRF-TAFC, a Grounded and Reflective Framework for Task-Adaptive Formation Choreography of CAVs. GRF-TAFC integrates context-grounded formation generation, optimization-based execution, and execution-driven reflection into a closed loop. A formation generator elicits the formation generation capabilities of pretrained MLLMs and grounds their reasoning over unstructured task inputs in real-time tool outputs, domain knowledge, and experience memory, yielding formations tailored to current task requirements while respecting environmental constraints. An execution module realizes the generated formations through polynomial-time CAV-to-target assignment and joint spatio-temporal trajectory optimization, facilitating collision avoidance and safe execution. A reflection module reasons over task context and actual execution outcomes, distilling reusable experience for iterative refinement. Real-world experiments across dynamic tasks and environments demonstrate GRF-TAFC’s effectiveness and practicality, with experimental videos available on the project website: https://dongjh20.github.io/GRF-TAFC.

papers.title: A physics-informed neural network for predicting vibration-induced human annoyance in over-track buildings
papers.abstract: Existing vibration assessment standards for over-track buildings are mainly based on vibration-limit criteria and do not explicitly account for nonlinear perceptual thresholds or individual differences in human sensitivity. To address this limitation, this study proposes a physics-informed neural-network framework for predicting vibration-induced human annoyance. The artificial intelligence contribution lies in incorporating monotonicity constraints and boundary conditions into the loss function, enabling the model to learn a physically consistent nonlinear relationship between vibration levels and human annoyance from survey data. The engineering application focuses on over-track buildings above a metro depot. A vehicle-track coupled model and a three-dimensional finite element model of the soil-track-depot-building system are developed to calculate the maximum Z-weighted vibration levels at key response points in different functional zones. These vibration responses are then used as inputs for spatial annoyance prediction. The results show that the proposed model achieves high predictive accuracy and good generalization, with a mean squared error below 0.01 and a coefficient of determination above 0.95 across all evaluated scenarios. The predicted annoyance decreases with lateral distance from the track in commercial buildings and with floor height in residential buildings. Compared with the Chinese national environmental vibration standard GB 10070-88, the proposed framework identifies localized annoyance exceedances even under nominally compliant vibration conditions and provides a continuous spatial distribution of vibration-induced environmental impacts.

papers.title: Predictive modelling of conducting Casson nanofluid flow using a physics-informed neural network: effects of thermal stratification and coupled transport mechanisms
papers.abstract: Conducting Casson nanofluid flow with thermal stratification plays vital role in advanced heat and mass transfer processes such as energy conversion, polymer processing, metallurgical operations, and biomedical applications. The simultaneous influence of magnetic fields, porous-medium resistance, Joule and Darcy dissipation, thermal radiation, Brownian motion, thermophoresis, and chemical reactions creates a strongly coupled nonlinear boundary-value problem that is difficult to solve using conventional analytical or numerical methods. To address this challenge, present study examines flow, heat-transfer, and mass-transfer behaviour of conducting Casson nanofluid over exponentially expanding permeable surface, incorporating thermal stratification along with aforementioned physical effects. Governing equations are reduced to a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations through similarity transformations. Physics-Informed Neural Network framework is developed to obtain predictive solutions by embedding the governing equations, boundary conditions and loss function. PINN utilizes automatic differentiation and a two-stage training strategy with Adam and L-BFGS optimizers. The numerical performance of the PINN is assessed using governing-equation residual metrics, including MSE, MAE, and RMSE. The MSE ranges from 4.74 × 10 −7 to 5.55 × 10 −3 , the MAE from 4.75 × 10 −4 to 5.32 × 10 −2 , and the RMSE from 6.89 × 10 −4 to 7.45 × 10 −2 across the reported parameter cases. These metrics quantify residual satisfaction of the governing equations rather than errors relative to an external reference solution. Agreement with an independently computed boundary-value solution is assessed separately through comparisons of the solution profiles and wall quantities for selected parameter cases. Overall, the results demonstrate the applicability of the PINN framework to the coupled nonlinear conducting Casson nanofluid problem. Independent comparison with a boundary-value solution was conducted for the baseline case and the parameter variations R d = 1.5 and S c = 0.6. The agreement in the wall quantities for these selected cases supports the numerical consistency of the PINN predictions under the conditions examined. These findings are limited to the evaluated cases and do not establish convergence or low solution error across the entire parameter range.

papers.title: AGAINST THE NATIVE JOINT MICROBIOME: UNIFORMLY NEGATIVE NGS IN HIP SYNOVIAL FLUID WITH PAIRED SALINE CONTROLS
papers.abstract: Introduction Humans exist in an intricate symbiotic relationship with host microbiome populations. It has been recently reported using Next Generation DNA Sequencing (NGS), that a native synovial joint microbiome may exist potentially contributing microbes in clinical infection. The counter argument is that synovial joints are sterile and positive detection reflects errant sampling and processing. We evaluate native hip synovial fluid sampled via a low-risk air-excluding technique incorporating paired saline controls and stringent NGS quality thresholds. Methods In this prospective cohort study, 40 consecutive patients undergoing primary Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA) for osteoarthritis were enrolled. All hips were approached via a posterolateral approach. Upon arthrotomy, hip fluid was directly aspirated with an 18-gauge needle into a 10cc syringe. Technique was meticulous not to aspirate any air. A concomitant control specimen was obtained by aspirating sterile saline from a freshly opened 100cc container on the operative field using an identical technique. All fluid aspirates were transferred into DNA-specific sterile vacutainers and sent overnight for NGS analysis. Results 40 hips were sampled, with one control specimen not sent with its corresponding test specimen. 16 hips were male (40%) and mean age was 67 years (range 41–89). All 40 synovial fluid specimens showed no significant DNA reads. All 39 saline control specimens showed no significant DNA reads. Conclusion Intraoperative NGS of 40 consecutive hip synovial fluid samples and all paired saline controls was uniformly negative using an air-excluding sampling technique, arguing against the existence of a native joint microbiome, a finding consistent with the teleologic principle of immunologic parsimony.

papers.title: Sequential rounding in mixed-integer model predictive control
papers.abstract: This paper interfaces combinatorial integral approximation strategies with the inherent robustness properties of conventional model predictive control with stabilizing terminal conditions to establish practical asymptotic stability results for finite control set and mixed-integer model predictive control. We examine the impact of sequential control rounding on the closed-loop performance in terms of stability and optimality. Sum-up rounding takes its decision on the basis of the integrated control approximation error and represents one instance of a sequential integer control reconstruction approach in combinatorial integral approximation. We first apply outer convexification and relaxation and then show how to embed the class of sequential rounding algorithms into the step-by-step operation of model predictive control. Numerical experiments serve to illustrate the importance of an advanced rounding strategy in the context of mixed-integer model predictive control.

papers.title: OUTCOMES OF FUNGAL VERSUS BACTERIAL PERIPROSTHETIC JOINT INFECTIONS AFTER TOTAL HIP AND KNEE ARTHROPLASTY: RETROSPECTIVE COHORT ANALYSIS OF 461 CASES
papers.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a rare but severe complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Bacterial pathogens account for most cases, while fungal PJIs represent approximately 1% and remain poorly characterized. The lack of direct and comparative studies between bacterial and fungal PJI makes it difficult to draw clear conclusions about differences in treatment outcomes, complication rates, and optimal management strategies. As a result, clinical decision-making for fungal PJIs is often extrapolated from bacterial PJI protocols, despite significant microbiologic differences. Aim This study compared outcomes of bacterial and fungal PJIs managed at a tertiary referral center. Methods We conducted a retrospective review of culture-proven bacterial and fungal PJIs involving THA or TKA at a single institution between January 2015 and February 2025. Diagnosis was based on Musculoskeletal Infection Society (MSIS) criteria. Demographics, comorbidities, infection chronicity, surgical strategy, and outcomes were collected. Treatment success was defined according to international Delphi consensus criteria. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify predictors of outcome. A total of 461 patients met inclusion criteria, including 402 bacterial and 59 fungal PJIs. Age, sex, and comorbidity profiles were similar between groups. Results Despite the similar baseline demographics, fungal infections more frequently presented as chronic (71% vs 52%, P = 0.013). In bivariate analysis, overall treatment success was significantly lower in fungal PJIs (22% vs 62%; OR 0.17 95% CI [0.09,0.33], P < 0.001). Mortality was higher in fungal infections (27% vs 11%; 2.97, [1.50,5.76], P = 0.002). Multivariable analysis identified fungal etiology, older age, higher Charlson Comorbidity Index, and current smoking as independent predictors for lower odds of success. When comparing treatment success by different surgical modalities, DAIR was particularly ineffective in fungal PJIs. Many of these DAIR procedures occurred before a fungal organism was identified. The prolonged incubation time required for fungal cultures delays definitive pathogen identification. Not only do fungal cultures take significantly longer to result, but there is significantly lower sensitivity compared to bacterial cultures. Thus, a DAIR procedure may be undertaken before fungal etiology is known, inadvertently applying a strategy that is ill- suited for fungal infections and contributing to their high failure rate. Conclusion Fungal PJIs are associated with markedly worse outcomes and higher mortality compared with bacterial infections. These findings emphasize the need for pathogen- specific surgical strategies, optimization of host comorbidities, and multicenter collaboration to standardize management of fungal PJIs.

papers.title: Overcoming brittleness in NbMoTaW refractory high entropy alloy: A review of strength–ductility strategies and challenges
papers.abstract: NbMoTaW and its derived refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) exhibiting a single body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice structure have attracted widespread attention due to their exceptional strength at high temperatures. However, their practical applications are limited by room-temperature brittleness. While the BCC stability ensures resistance to thermal softening, its intrinsic high barrier to dislocation movements reduces the intrinsic ductility. Extensive research has been focused on mitigating this issue through microstructural and compositional modification. This review first discusses the fundamental mechanisms governing the brittleness in NbMoTaW and related BCC RHEAs, including grain boundary embrittlement, intrinsic properties and atomic environments. Then promising results from alloying and processing optimization are highlighted. Finally, the industrial feasibility and potential directions for alloy design and development are outlined.

papers.title: Combining shear wave elastography and ultrasound localization microscopy for liver fibrosis staging in a rat model
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective Accurate staging of liver fibrosis (LF) remains a clinical challenge. This study aimed to quantitatively evaluate the diagnostic value of combining shear wave elastography (SWE) and ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) for LF staging across the full disease spectrum. We sought to integrate liver mechanical properties and microvascular structural parameters to build a multiparametric model for fibrosis staging. Materials and methods LF was induced in Sprague–Dawley rats and histologically staged according to the METAVIR system. A total of 62 rats were included in the final analysis. Both SWE and ULM were performed in each animal. Liver viscoelastic moduli were estimated from SWE data using SW-VEI-Net, a physics-informed neural network-based approach. ULM data were post-processed to reconstruct super-resolution images of the hepatic microvasculature, followed by quantitative analysis to extract microvascular structural parameters. Results Histology revealed fibrosis stages F0 ( n = 10), F1 ( n = 12), F2 ( n = 19), F3 ( n = 11), and F4 ( n = 10). Compared with the single-modality SWE and ULM models, the multiparametric combined model achieved the highest numerical areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve across the four classification tasks: 0.93 for F0 versus F1–F4, 0.92 for F0–F1 versus F2–F4, 0.90 for F0–F2 versus F3–F4, and 0.89 for F0–F3 versus F4. Conclusion Combining SWE-derived viscoelastic parameters with ULM-derived microvascular features enabled multiparametric characterization of LF in this preclinical rat model. Independent validation in larger animal cohorts and, ultimately, human studies is essential before robust clinical conclusions can be drawn. Key Points Question Can combining shear-wave elastography (SWE) and ULM improve the accuracy of LF staging? Findings By integrating viscoelastic and microvascular features, the SWE-ULM combined model achieved the highest numerical AUCs across all four fibrosis classifications in a rat model. Relevance statement The SWE and ULM combined model suggests potential value for LF staging by integrating viscoelastic and microvascular biomarkers, providing a basis for further investigation toward future clinical translation.

papers.title: Multi-agent path planning and reinforcement learning for wire harness handling
papers.abstract: Wire harness manufacturing remains one of the most labor-intensive parts of automotive production, with the “form and tape” assembly process constituting the key bottleneck. Emerging industrial concepts shift automation from single-wire routing to module-based forming. This leads to a multi-agent planning and control problem in which moving connector housing fixtures are strongly coupled by the partially formed harness. The contact-rich and highly variable behavior of the wires as linear deformable objects is difficult to model analytically. We investigate two planning and control paradigms within a MuJoCo-based simulation environment with a Gymnasium-compatible interface. First, we use multi-agent path planning ideas on continuous, cable-coupled motion via prioritized planning with heuristic guidance and reactive constraint checking, yielding a 78% overall success rate for the best planner configuration. Second, we apply reinforcement learning, both standalone and as a residual on top of a geometric base policy, comparing SAC, PPO, and TRPO. Surprisingly, the best results are achieved by plain end-to-end SAC, which reaches a mean overall success rate of 98% (range: 95%–99%) and solves nearly 114 of 120 complete target permutation, against 65 for the best planner, whereas residual RL, despite its greater stability on single transitions, fails to generalize to the full sequence of target configurations. The results indicate a central trade-off between rule-based algorithmic planning and learned control in wire harness handling. The simulation environment is publicly available at: https://github.com/ludwigstr/WireHarness-MultiAgent-RL .

papers.title: Dynamic KNX-based energy management system with machine learning for energy optimization
papers.abstract: Efficient energy management in residential buildings is essential for reducing consumption and supporting sustainability initiatives. Conventional Energy Management Systems (EMS) often rely on static control strategies that do not reflect dynamic occupancy patterns, limiting their capacity to optimize performance. This study presents a dynamic KNX-based EMS that integrates real-time occupancy sensing with machine learning models to support forecast-assisted energy management of building energy systems. A residential building in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, equipped with a 200-kW photovoltaic array and a 100-kW inverter, was simulated using HOMER Pro. High-resolution data from lighting, HVAC, and occupancy sensors were analyzed separately and compared after hourly aggregation to characterize building energy demand. The Solace dataset was then separated into 70% training and 30% testing subsets for ML model development and validation. Four predictive models: Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GBM), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) were trained and tuned using Bayesian optimization and five-fold cross-validation. The integration of KNX occupancy controls resulted in an average hourly energy reduction of 15.33% over the 41-day monitoring period relative to the HOMER baseline, while the SVR-predicted annual energy consumption was 313,239.12 kWh, corresponding to a difference of 61,798.88 kWh (16.48%) relative to the HOMER baseline. Among the evaluated models, RF achieved the highest large-scale accuracy, while SVR offered the best balance between accuracy and computational cost at the moderate data scale. These findings suggest that integrating dynamic KNX automation with machine learning supports forecast-assisted, data-driven energy management of residential energy systems, providing a scalable strategy for enhancing energy efficiency in smart buildings.

papers.title: A transformative pedagogical model for architectural design education in Ethiopia through studio based practice
papers.abstract: This study explores the implementation of a Transformative Practice-Based Pedagogical Model (TPM) in architectural design education in Ethiopia, aiming to integrate research, theory, and practice within a studio-based learning environment. The model was applied to a full cohort of third-year architecture students ( n = 20) at Arba Minch University, using the Evaluation–Creation Cycle (ECC) as a design research methodology in combination with active learning strategies. The study responds to limitations in conventional design studio pedagogy, which often emphasizes instructor-centered and product-oriented approaches that may constrain critical engagement and contextual responsiveness. A baseline assessment, drawing on students’ prior experiences in Architectural Design Studio I under a traditional instructional approach, informed the TPM-based intervention. The model was implemented through a structured four-phase process involving information gathering, empirical case analysis, theory–practice integration, and design development. Findings indicate improvements in students’ reflective thinking, engagement with research-informed design processes, and the contextual grounding of design outcomes. Given the single-cohort design and absence of a parallel control group, the findings are preliminary and context-specific; future research to further examine the model’s effectiveness across different architectural education contexts. The study contributes initial empirical insights into the potential of context-responsive pedagogical frameworks with TPM model, for architectural education in Ethiopia and similar Global South contexts.

papers.title: Material-dependent viscoelastic performance of TPU and PEBA gyroid intervertebral disc replacements under quasi-static and cyclic compression
papers.abstract: Thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) and polyether block amide (PEBA) offer different mechanical profiles for additively manufactured intervertebral disc replacements. This study compared single-material Gyroid structures with the same nominal anatomically derived L4/L5 geometry using a harmonized secondary analysis of original specimen-level datasets. Geometry #08 comprised a 6 mm unit-cell size and a nominal wall thickness of 0.75 mm without a peripheral wall. FlexHard and FlexMed TPU and Spectrum and SainSmart PEBA were investigated. Three additional unloaded reference specimens per material underwent dimensional, gravimetric, and microscopic characterization. FlexHard, FlexMed, and Spectrum met the predefined quasi-static screening criterion of 4000–8000 N at 50% compression, whereas SainSmart remained below 4000 N and was not dynamically tested. Eligible groups completed 700,000 compression cycles between 600 and 2000 N at 5 Hz without apparent mechanical failure (n = 3 per material). Outcomes were evaluated over the final 600,000 cycles following 100,000 conditioning cycles. Structural stiffness increased by 16.1% for FlexHard and 76.5% for FlexMed but decreased by 10.6% for Spectrum. Apparent storage modulus increased by 30.9% and 44.1% in the TPU groups and decreased by 10.3% in Spectrum. Mean loss modulus increased in both TPU groups and decreased in Spectrum, although within-material changes were not significant after multiplicity adjustment. Tan δ and specific damping capacity decreased in all three groups, with both TPU formulations maintaining higher mean damping capacities than Spectrum. Immediately after loading, TPU specimens retained approximately 90% of their initial height, compared with approximately 95% for Spectrum; all groups recovered to approximately 97%–99% after 24 h. These exploratory findings identify complementary profiles in load support, energy dissipation, cyclic adaptation, and recovery. Because manufacturing conditions differed between source datasets, the results characterize the investigated material–manufacturing combinations and support joint optimization of formulation, processing, and architecture.

papers.title: SAFE-AD: Socially aware field-enhanced reinforcement learning for autonomous driving in interactive traffic
papers.abstract: Abstract An autonomous vehicle can complete its route while disrupting surrounding traffic. We introduce SAFE-AD, augmenting reinforcement learning (RL) observations with compact descriptors of a finite-horizon interaction-pressure field constructed from current traffic states. The complete objective supplements the environment's task reward with risk, comfort, and externality costs. Then, we formulate a context-conditioned physics-informed neural network (PINN) to approximate the numerical field. Evaluation combines held-out naturalistic recordings, HighwayEnv diagnostics, and closed-loop MetaDrive tests in various traffic scenarios, with a matched factorial experiment with continuous soft actor-critic (SAC) separates observation and objective effects. At unprotected intersections, the complete profile reduces collision rate from 0.296 to 0.220 and mean absolute jerk by 0.98 m/s3 relative to baseline SAC. Besides, the mean absolute jerk in roundabout decreases by 1.54 m/s3. The results show scenario-specific gains and sensitivity to objective calibration.

papers.title: Mussels possess distinct vanadium and iron storage systems for fabricating metal-reinforced adhesive fibers
papers.abstract: Mussels fashion a protein-based fibrous adhesive holdfast known as a byssus to tether themselves in marine habitats against crashing waves. The capacity of mussels to anchor securely is dependent on load-bearing protein-metal cross-links mediated by 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (DOPA) residues coordinated to metal ions, which significantly enhance byssus mechanical properties (e.g., adhesive strength, abrasion resistance, toughness, self-healing capacity). However, the natural metal incorporation process during byssus formation remains poorly understood—a knowledge gap that limits the decades-old field of mussel-inspired materials from fulfilling its potential. Here, we investigate the natural byssus biofabrication system, the mussel foot, focusing specifically on iron and vanadium storage using a multilength scale ensemble of spectroscopic methods. Confocal Raman spectroscopy, synchrotron µ-X-ray fluorescence and µ-X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and scanning transmission electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy studies indicate that these two metals occupy separate coordination environments: vanadium storage is DOPA-based, while iron is stored in ferritin-like structures. Lacking precedence, these findings indicate that mussels evolved a catechol-based metal storage system to specifically acquire and store what is typically considered a trace metal ion in biology, which they employ subsequently to mechanically reinforce protein-based glues and coatings produced by the mussel. Beyond the biological implications, these findings have potential to transform the field of mussel-inspired materials.

papers.title: Intelligent Prediction of High-Enthalpy Gas Environments for Arc Heaters Based on the Bayesian Optimization Attention-Aware Network and Transfer Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract Arc heaters are the core devices for simulating the aerothermal environment of hypersonic vehicles. To meet the demand for rapid and high-accuracy prediction of the high-enthalpy gas environment in segmented arc heaters, this study proposes an intelligent prediction method based on a Bayesian Optimization Attention-Aware Network (B-AAN) integrated with transfer learning. First, a feature-attention module is embedded into a multilayer perceptron to perform sample-dependent reweighting of the input features before they are passed to the shared multi-output prediction network. Subsequently, Bayesian optimization is employed to tune the model’s hyperparameters. Meanwhile, SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis is introduced to reveal the contribution mechanisms of different input features to the prediction results. Finally, a model transfer strategy is further incorporated to address the prediction of high-enthalpy gas environments under new operating conditions. The proposed model was validated using a multi-operating-condition database established from an arc heater experimental platform. The results show that, under conditions of different model initialization random seeds and fixed data partitions, this method achieves high prediction accuracy for arc voltage, arc chamber pressure, and enthalpy, with prediction errors below 3%. The transfer learning results further indicate that the model can still maintain high prediction accuracy and stability after fine-tuning with only a limited number of samples under new operating conditions. Compared with conventional machine learning methods, the method proposed in this paper provides more balanced predictive performance across the three outputs. Overall, the proposed B-AAN method combined with transfer learning provides an effective solution for the intelligent operation and maintenance of arc heaters.

papers.title: Multi-hazard road-network criticality from earth observation data using spatial graph attention networks with conformal uncertainty
papers.abstract: Coastal deltaic road networks in India experience compounding hazards of monsoon flooding, prolonged soil-moisture saturation, and heat stress. However, many graph-learning approaches to network vulnerability assessment validate with random train–test splits that do not account for spatial dependence between adjacent road segments leading to insufficient quantification of failure probability without any spatially calibrated uncertainty. This study attempts to address these gaps by developing a spatially aware Graph Attention Network (GAT) that estimates road-segment failure probability from multi-hazard exposure and network-topological covariates. Due to the lack of geocoded road-closure records, multi-hazard threshold rules were used to generate training labels, with model predictions interpreted as disruption susceptibility rather than observed failure probabilities. Model performance was evaluated using random and spatial-block cross-validation, while split-conformal prediction was used to quantify predictive uncertainty. The framework was applied to the East Godavari–Krishna deltaic corridor of coastal Andhra Pradesh using multi-source climate, satellite, terrain, road-network and population data (i.e., IMD, NASA SMAP, ERA5-Land, CHIRPS, Copernicus DEM, Sentinel-2, OpenStreetMap, and WorldPop) from 2016 to 2025. The GAT achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.923 ± 0.001 under random cross-validation, and 0.682 ± 0.126 under spatial-block cross-validation. Under spatial-block cross-validation, Random Forest outperformed the GAT in all five folds, achieving an AUC of 0.746 ± 0.134 using the same edge-level features without network topology. Message-passing ablation indicated a marginal improvement from real network topology, with an AUC of 0.639 without message passing compared with 0.624 using randomly shuffled neighbours. A population-weighted Monte Carlo simulation showed that failure-probability-weighted removal produced greater network efficiency loss than random removal across all tested removal fractions (1%–20%), with the largest difference observed at 10% removal, where the loss ratio reached 1.65 times. A consequence-sensitive risk ranking combining failure probability and demand-weighted network flow identified a top 5% of segments whose protection avoided 56% of simulated accessibility loss, compared with 15% for failure-probability ranking, 18% for hazard-exposure ranking, and 43% for edge betweenness.

papers.title: Machine Learning Driven Hybrid Surrogate Modeling and NSGA-II Optimization of Machining Performance Parameters
papers.abstract: A hybrid surrogate modeling and machine-learning framework was designed for EN31 alloy turning to explore the machining performance in liquid CO 2 assisted minimum quantity lubrication (MQL). The effect of flow rate, cutting velocity and depth of cut on material removal rate (MRR), surface roughness (Ra), rake-face temperature rise (Trake) and cutting force were modeled by using 18 observations obtained experimentally. Models were comparatively evaluated using nested Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV) with model-specific hyperparameter optimization, i.e., Linear Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). The updated results show the predictive performance depending on the response. ANN provided the best baseline prediction for MRR and Ra, whereas SVR achieved the best prediction among the baseline models for Trake and cutting forceThe hybrid surrogate model, consisting of second-order polynomial trend and Gaussian Process residual learning, obtained R 2 values of 0.9882, 0.8560, 0.9901 and 0.9877 for MRR, Ra, Trake and cutting force respectively. Sensitivity analysis, predictive uncertainty quantification, and quantitative SHAP analysis were used to increase the interpretability of model predictions. Finally, NSGA-II was used for simultaneous maximization of MRR and minimization of Ra, Trake and cutting force in the experimentally investigated domain of parameters. The Pareto solutions obtained provide alternative machining conditions according to productivity, surface quality, thermal response and mechanical loading requirements. Thus, the proposed framework offers an interpretable, data-efficient approach for predictive modeling and multi-objective decision making in sustainable machining.

papers.title: Comparaison de la compacité d’échangeurs de chaleur dans le cadre d’un réacteur à sels fondus
papers.abstract: L’avancée de la fabrication additive permet la conception de nouvelles géométries d’échangeurs de chaleur. Parmi elles, les échangeurs à surfaces dites TPMS Schwarz-diamant présentent un intérêt pour les réacteurs à sels fondus qui nécessitent des échangeurs de chaleurs compacts à faible risque d’encrassement. Cette étude vise à quantifier le gain de compacité d’un tel échangeur vis-à-vis d’un échangeur tubes et calandre, c’est-à-dire comparer le volume de sel fondu mobilisé côté primaire, dans une situation de fonctionnement fixée. La comparaison est effectuée à iso-puissance échangée, iso-températures, iso-débits, iso-diamètres hydrauliques et, iso-perte de charge coté primaire. La méthode présentée s’appuie sur les équations établies par Webb basées sur la conservation du coefficient d’échange global et de la puissance de pompage. Une équation supplémentaire est établie pour la conservation du rapport des débits entre les deux passes de chaque échangeur. A partir des corrélations existantes et dans le domaine de fonctionnement d’intérêt, la méthode montre un gain important de compacité apporté par les échangeurs TPMS par rapport à l’échangeur tubes et calandre.

papers.title: Leveraging transport theory to advance machine learning for weather forecasting
papers.abstract: Transport processes govern the evolution of many physical systems, including atmospheric dynamics, where information, mass, energy, and uncertainty propagate across space and time. Although machine learning has achieved remarkable success in forecasting complex spatiotemporal phenomena, many existing models rely on local operators and pointwise objectives that inadequately capture the transport mechanisms underlying physical processes. This limitation is particularly pronounced in weather forecasting, where accurate prediction requires modeling both the movement of meteorological structures and the evolution of uncertainty across multiple spatial and temporal scales. This thesis investigates how principles from transport theory can be leveraged to develop machine learning models that are more accurate and physically grounded. The central premise of this thesis is that transport provides a unifying framework for learning spatiotemporal dynamics. Rather than treating forecasting as a purely statistical prediction problem, we develop learning architectures that explicitly model the transport of information, features, and probability distributions. Building on concepts from partial differential equations, dynamical systems, and generative modeling, we propose transport-aware methods for both deterministic and probabilistic forecasting. The contributions of this thesis are twofold. First, we introduce transport-aware neural architectures based on advection-diffusion-reaction dynamics, incorporating a semi-Lagrangian transport operator that enables efficient non-local information propagation in convolutional neural networks. Second, the state-of-the-art probabilistic models are based on stochastic diffusion models that are expensive and also not naturally suitable for sensitive dynamical systems. We extend transport concepts to probabilistic forecasting by formulating uncertainty quantification as a distributional transport problem and developing flow-matching-based methods that learn transport maps between probability distributions, enabling faster generation of physically consistent ensemble forecasts. Experiments on benchmark spatiotemporal datasets, including weather forecasting applications, demonstrate improvements in predictive accuracy, long-range information propagation, uncertainty calibration, and physical consistency. Collectively, the results establish transport theory as a powerful organizing principle for machine learning and provide a general framework for incorporating physically motivated transport mechanisms into forecasting systems and other scientific machine learning applications.

papers.title: Applying Self-Organizing Kohonen Maps to the Traveling Salesman Problem
papers.abstract: This paper discusses solving the traveling salesman problem using Kohonen maps. We investigate the application of Self-Organizing Maps (SOM) to the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP), develop Central Processing Unit (CPU)- and Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)-based implementations of the proposed approach, and evaluate their efficiency in SOM hyperparameter tuning using a multistage dimensionality reduction framework and Bayesian optimization. Bayesian optimization based on sequential trial selection was used to select the parameters. A new SOM configuration was defined for each trial, after which the map was trained, and the objective function value was calculated. This approach differs from exhaustive searches in that subsequent trials are selected based on the results already obtained.

papers.title: Clinical Success, Mechanical Stability, and Peri-Implant Radiographic Characteristics of Orthodontic Mini-Screws Under Immediate Versus Delayed Loading: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical success, mechanical stability, and peri-implant radiographic characteristics of orthodontic mini-screws subjected to immediate loading (IL) versus delayed loading (DL). METHODS: This retrospective comparative study evaluated the clinical records of 100 orthodontic patients who received one orthodontic mini-screw in the maxilla or mandible. Implant stability was assessed using the Implant Stability Quotient (ISQ) and Periotest values (PTV) at baseline and at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Peri-implant radiographic measurements were obtained using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) at the documented assessment time points. Failures included screw loss, mobility > grade 1, persistent inflammation > 2 weeks, or pain requiring removal. Survival was analyzed with Kaplan-Meier curves. RESULTS: Clinical success was recorded in 47 of 50 mini-screws (94.0%) in the IL group and 46 of 50 (92.0%) in the DL group, with 3 and 4 documented failures, respectively. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to assess time to clinical failure. ISQ values showed a transient decrease at 1 month in both groups, followed by progressive recovery and stabilization by 6 months. PTV values changed inversely to ISQ, showing a corresponding temporary increase at 1 month and subsequent improvement thereafter. CBCT-measured peri-implant bone density increased progressively at 6, 12, and 24 months compared with baseline in both groups. Insertion torque and removal torque values were similar between the two loading protocols. CONCLUSIONS: Immediate and delayed loading of orthodontic mini-screws were associated with similar observed clinical success proportions and mechanical stability measurements, with no clear between-group differences in the available peri-implant radiographic findings. These results do not establish equivalence between loading protocols or directly demonstrate histological osseointegration.

papers.title: Metaphyseal Sleeves for Bone Defects in Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The management of metaphyseal bone defect constitutes a persistent challenge in revision total knee arthroplasty (RTKA). Metaphyseal sleeves achieve fixation through biologic press fit and have been increasingly utilized for managing severe bone defects. While individual series have reported favorable outcomes, an integrated and systematic synthesis of the current evidence remains unavailable. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library was conducted from inception through March 30, 2026. Studies were considered eligible if they reported clinical, radiographic, or survivorship outcomes using metaphyseal sleeves in RTKA. Data extracted included patient demographics, implant details, function, survivorship, and radiographic outcomes. All pooled estimates were calculated using random-effects models, and subgroup analyses were performed according to fixation method and duration of follow-up. A total of 41 studies comprising 3,037 knees and 4,774 sleeves were included. RESULTS: The pooled postoperative Knee Society Score Knee score was 90.9 points (95% confidence interval [CI], 82.6 to 99.3), and the pooled maximal knee flexion was 108.3° (95% CI, 102.2 to 114.5). The rate of all-cause re-revision was 6.5% (95% CI, 4.2 to 9.2), with periprosthetic joint infection identified as the leading cause of failure. Sleeve removal for aseptic loosening occurred in 0.1% (95% CI, 0 to 0.4) of sleeves, and the rate of osseointegration was 99.6% (95% CI, 98.5 to 100). There was no statistically significant difference in sleeve removal for aseptic loosening between uncemented and hybrid fixation or between the ≤ 36 months and greater than 36 months groups. CONCLUSIONS: Metaphyseal sleeves in RTKA are associated with low rates of aseptic loosening and high rates of radiographic osseointegration, with periprosthetic joint infection remaining the predominant cause of failure. Sleeve survival appears independent of fixation method and is maintained over the duration of follow-up. Further studies with surveillance beyond 10 years and direct comparative investigations between sleeves and alternative metaphyseal fixation methods are warranted.

papers.title: Numerical investigation of the fatigue crack growth path in Ti-6Al-4V alloy material
papers.abstract: The primary objective of this numerical investigation is to simulate and foresee the crack propagation behavior in linear elastic materials subjected to mixed-mode (Mode I + Mode II) loading, with specific focus on understanding the influence of geometric discontinuities (holes) on the fatigue life and crack growth in Modified Compact Tension Specimens (MCTS). Leveraging principles from Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM), the study employs the Paris’ Law model to quantitatively evaluate the fatigue crack growth behavior in Ti-6Al-4V alloy specimens featuring multiple geometric configurations. The computational methodology incorporates, progressive crack growth analysis under cyclic loading conditions, fatigue life prediction based on crack length increment and cycle count, accurate calculation of Stress Intensity Factors (SIF’s) for mixed-mode conditions and fracture path trajectory simulation based on energy release rate and local stress field. Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is conducted using ANSYS, enabling precise prediction of crack propagation paths and corresponding fatigue life under constant amplitude cyclic loading. The effect of hole placement and spacing (i.e. various MCTS configurations) is systematically examined to assess their role in altering the stress concentration, crack deflection, and fatigue crack growth rate. This study provides critical insights into the design sensitivity of MCTS geometries in high-cycle fatigue environments and supports the optimization of damage-tolerant structures through advanced fracture modeling techniques.

papers.title: Hybrid retrieval method for leaf chlorophyll content mapping of winter wheat from EnMAP spaceborne imaging spectroscopy data
papers.abstract: Accurate mapping of leaf chlorophyll content (Cab) is critical for monitoring plant growth and maximising crop yields in sustainable precision farming. This study developed a nonparametric, hybrid retrieval method to map winter wheat (Triticum aestivum) Cab from EnMAP spaceborne hyperspectral data, using in situ data collected in southern Hungary. A simulated training dataset was optimised using principal component analysis, active learning (AL), and spectral and sampling reduction, then used to train a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model. Validation yielded R² = 0.76 and RMSE = 8.22 μg/cm². The best results were achieved after adding 101 AL samples to 50 starting samples (NRMSE = 15.72%). Adding non-vegetated (NV) spectra slightly reduced validation accuracy (NRMSE = 16.93%, R² = 0.74) but produced more consistent models able to handle spectral variability across the heterogeneous EnMAP scene. GPR also provides uncertainty estimates alongside trait retrievals, indicating model reliability.

papers.title: A fuzzy DEMATEL–ISM framework for unpacking barriers to digital twin adoption in high-density crowd management
papers.abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology promises to revolutionize the management of large gatherings by coupling physical assets with their virtual counterparts to enable real–time situational awareness. However, adoption in safety–critical crowd scenarios remains limited. This work introduces a hybrid framework combining fuzzy Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (FDEMATEL) and Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) to systematically identify, interrelate, and prioritize the obstacles to DT deployment for hyper–dense events such as Hajj and Umrah. By embedding fuzzy logic, the method captures the vagueness and variability of expert assessments, while ISM organizes barriers into a hierarchical structure. Analysis of ten barriers (BR1–BR10) identifies the nascent stage of domain implementation (BR10) as the deepest root cause, occupying the base of the interpretive structural hierarchy and exhibiting the largest net causal effect. The shortage of specialized expertise (BR6) occupies the second hierarchical level, mediating between domain immaturity and the remaining barriers. Crowd dynamics and behavioral diversity, legacy system integration, and regulatory and governance frameworks are net causes in the DEMATEL sense but occupy the upper hierarchical level as members of a mutually reinforcing cluster. Infrastructure requirements and cost emerge as the most strongly dependent barriers, followed by resistance to change and privacy concerns. The findings invert the intervention priorities transferred from industrial digital twin deployment, where cost and infrastructure are treated as binding constraints, and provide a cause-and-effect roadmap for policymakers and technology providers.

papers.title: Virtual viscometer based on Physics-Informed mCRE formulation using Deep-Learning with Finite-Volume Multiple-Mesh Training. Part I: steady flow CNN-augmented Reduced-Order Model
papers.abstract: Fluid rheology law identification requires viscometers in order to identify material parameters characterizing kinematic properties. Among these parameters the viscosity is a key factor since it is associated with shear stress effects and describes resistance of liquids to fluid flow according to friction occuring inside the medium during motion. However identification of viscosity often remains a difficulty due to the noise disturbing measurements that have to be filtered in a way to be defined. Moreover parameter inverse identification is most of the time associated with ill-posed problems resulting in a non-unicity of solutions, especially in the presence of strong shear effects. In the present work, a Physics-Informed Neural Network Architecture (mCRE-based PINN) is introduced as a Reduced-Order Model (ROM) in order to create a virtual viscometer in order to deal with viscosity identification in homogeneous and heterogeneousenvironments. A modified Constitutive-Relation Error (mCRE) is involved in order to enforce structural physical consistency of solutions and the proposed approach relies on a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that projects noisy velocity fields onto a low-dimensional space of physically admissible solutions. To ensure robust parameter identification, the modified mCRE framework acts as a physical constraint within the Artificial Neural Network (NN) Architecture. Unlike purely Data-Driven Methods (DDM), this hybrid approach provides a Physics-Informed ROM of fluid behavior that can be used as a virtual viscometer by minimizing the constitutive residual, effectively filtering out data noise while enforcing the underlying physical laws. A parameter sensitivity analysis is performed here in order to highlight the strength of the mCRE-based neural operator providing better accuracy and robustness for inverse viscosity identification than standard regression-based ROMs. The way Deep Learning (DL) is combined with physical constraints provides a powerful approach towards more reliable and interpretable surrogate modelling that may be appropriate in the context of Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). This new generation of Physics-Informed NN-based ROM will make it possible in a near future to gain efficiency for in-situ real-time flow field monitoring and control thanks to robust optimized multi-parameter meta-models.

papers.title: Next-generation process monitoring and control for metal additive manufacturing: toward a physics-informed digital twin framework
papers.abstract: Metal additive manufacturing (MAM) enables fabrication of geometrically complex components but faces process-induced defects that undermine quality consistency. The digital twin (DT) paradigm, a synchronised virtual counterpart of the physical process, offers a powerful framework for intelligent closed-loop quality assurance. However, MAM-DT’s full potential is limited by the divide between its two foundational modelling approaches: physics-based models offer accuracy but are computationally prohibitive for real-time use, while data-driven models are fast yet require extensive data and lack physical interpretability. Physics-informed machine learning (PIML) emerges as the pivotal technology for their fusion. This review first elaborates a four-layer MAM-DT system architecture. It then critically examines the virtual twin’s two pillars: accelerated physics-based and surrogate modelling, and data-driven in-situ monitoring and control, highlighting their limitations. The core contribution is a systematic taxonomy and analysis of PIML methodologies, categorised as Physics-Augmented Data, Physics-Constrained Learning, and Physics-Guided Architecture, which serve as the core fusion engine for MAM-DT. Their principles, applications in MAM, and roles in enhancing generalizability, data efficiency, and physical plausibility are detailed. Finally, the paper concludes with a critical discussion of current challenges and future research directions, outlining a path toward autonomous, self-optimizing, trustworthy intelligent manufacturing systems.

papers.title: Quality by Design Strategies for Bioequivalent Generic Immediate- and Sustained-Release Tablets: A Practical Development Roadmap
papers.abstract: Quality by Design (QbD) provides a science- and risk-based framework for developing generic immediate-release (IR) and sustained-release (SR) tablets. Its practical value, however, depends on translating formulation and process knowledge into evidence supporting bioequivalence (BE), manufacturing robustness, and regulatory decisions. This review presents a practical development roadmap integrating reference listed drug characterization, critical material attributes, critical process parameters, Design of Experiments (DoE), dissolution assessment, BE strategy, design-space justification, and scale-up verification. Its distinctive contribution is an evidence-to-decision framework combining sequential development gates with an evidence hierarchy that distinguishes experimental observations, model-derived inferences, and product-level conclusions. The review compares IR and SR development priorities, including potential Biopharmaceutics Classification System-based biowaivers for eligible IR products and polymer attributes, dissolution kinetics, food effects, and dose-dumping risks for SR formulations. Quantitative case studies illustrate formulation optimization, dissolution modelling, process analytical technology, and commercial-scale assessment, while highlighting the limitations of individual studies in establishing BE or generalized improvements in development efficiency and manufacturing robustness. Artificial intelligence, Bayesian optimization, and continuous manufacturing are critically examined, with emphasis on model validation, independent confirmation, clinically relevant dissolution testing, and representative scale-up evidence. The proposed roadmap supports systematic experimental planning, evidence interpretation, and scientifically justified development and regulatory decisions for generic IR and SR tablets.

papers.title: Formulation‐Driven Design of Antimicrobial Hydrogel Wound Patches 3D‐Printed by Digital Light Processing: Mapping Polysaccharide and Nanoparticle Effects
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Wound dressings must balance antimicrobial efficacy with the printability limits imposed by nanoparticle‐mediated ultraviolet attenuation during digital light processing 3D printing. Here, we develop process–structure–property relationships for poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA)‐based hydrogel wound patches containing Ag/ZnO‐derived antimicrobial phases and polysaccharide/cellulose modifiers (cellulose nanofibrils, chitosan, or alginate). Beer–Lambert analysis shows that nanoparticle loading reduces optical penetration depth at 405 nm to 1.04‐1.28 mm, narrowing the usable curing margin so that radiant exposure exceeds the critical energy by only 4%–5%. Flory–Rehner analysis of swelling reveals formulation‐dependent crosslink density: alginate lowers effective crosslink density by 45% vs. neat PEGDA and increases mesh size from 0.42 to 0.60 nm. This network loosening drives 1.5× variation in water vapor transmission rate (WVTR; 346–518 g·m − 2 ·day − 1 ) and a 7× range in wettability (11.5°–81.1°). Two‐way factorial analysis identifies polysaccharide type as the dominant driver of swelling (87.5% of variance) and antimicrobial efficacy (>50%), while nanoparticle type controls contact angle (60.1%) and WVTR (76.9%). The Ag + chitosan formulation (S5) achieves 23–24 mm inhibition zones against Escherichia coli and Bacillus sp. via chitosan‐facilitated Ag + diffusion plus intrinsic contact‐killing. Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy confirms cumulative Ag + release (32.7 mg·L − 1 over 14 days), while Zn 2 + remains immobilized below detection.

papers.title: Rare earth elements and additive manufacturing: a review
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) has enabled unprecedented design freedom in the fabrication of complex metallic and ceramic geometries; however, many traditional feedstocks are not well-suited for AM, and the incorporation of rare earth elements (REEs) has become increasingly important in improving printability, controlling solidification, refining microstructures, and enhancing end-use performance. Development of AM-tailored materials is necessary to meet the requirements of industrial applications. High-performance materials containing REEs offer unique properties, such as high corrosion resistance and superior mechanical strength, though these elements pose challenges, including limited availability. This review provides a thorough overview of the current state-of-the-art in AM of high-performance metallic and ceramic feedstocks containing REEs, with an emphasis on the interactions with AM processes and final structure performance. The behaviour of high-performance materials containing REEs under the processing conditions in various AM is explored based on the most recent literature. The benefits, challenges, and opportunities associated with metallic and ceramic AM feedstocks containing REEs are discussed. The mechanics of next-generation materials and microstructural features are reviewed and analysed. A roadmap of research gaps, functional applications, industrial adoption, and societal needs is presented with regard to the integration of REEs to enhance structures fabricated via AM processes.

papers.title: Methods for the Automation of Subject Indexing from Simple Statistical to Large Language Models – a Case Study
papers.abstract: Subject indexing, i.e., the enrichment of metadata records for textual resources with descriptors from a controlled vocabulary, is one of the core activities of libraries. Due to the proliferation of digital documents, it is no longer possible to annotate every single document intellectually, which is why libraries need to explore the potentials of automation on every level, up to and including methods from artificial intelligence (AI). While the current hype around deep learning approaches such as large language models (LLMs) has brought an unprecedented level of attention from the general public to AI, models from other branches of AI that were open source and showed potential for practical applications already started emerging over a decade ago. In this case study, we are investigating open source machine learning methods that are currently being used or evaluated in libraries for the automation of subject indexing, from statistical and lexical models to approaches that are based on transformer architectures, i.e., small and large language models. We present a selection of experimental results with regard to how well these models perform on typical bibliographic metadata of a library and draw conclusions on some of the difficulties surrounding the sizes and characteristics of bibliographic datasets as training data and what would have to be done in order to remedy the situation. We also describe possible measures for monitoring the quality of the output of such models, including automated solutions and approaches that integrate humans into the loop of quality control at various points. One promising approach is active learning, in which a coordinating algorithm decides which kind of input data would be most useful for training when annotated intellectually. Methods like these might gradually change the role of scientific librarians, which is why it is paramount to work together with subject indexing experts not only to ensure good quality output, but also to foster transparency and acceptance.

papers.title: Freeform 3D Printing of Omnidirectionally Deformable Conductors via Newtonian Liquid Metal Droplet‐Mediated Stress Relaxation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Next‐generation soft robotics and shape‐morphing electronics demand materials that possess intrinsic softness yet processable into freeform 3D architectures. However, direct‐write 3D printing of soft elastomers suffers from a rheological trade‐off, where high yield stress required for printability increases stiffness. This work presents a ternary silicone elastomer ink that breaks this limitation by incorporating liquid metal (LM) as a Newtonian liquid filler. The fluidic LM droplets act as stress buffers, accelerating stress relaxation during flow without compromising post‐curing compliance. Additionally, they induce an excluded‐volume effect that increases the effective local concentration of the dispersed multi‐walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), thereby enhancing the percolating conductive network. This strategy enables support‐free 3D printing, achieving maximum bridging spans of 32 mm and a peak resolution of 124 µm independently. The composite exhibits high stretchability (446% elongation), a bulk conductivity of 7.08 S/m, and electrical stability under large deformation (∆R/R 0 = 0.51 at 100% strain). The versatility of this platform was further validated through reconfigurable 3D circuits, demonstrating that in addition to functioning as compliant conductors, the printed structures can also serve as robust load‐bearing structural elements. By reconciling printability, softness, and deformation‐tolerant electrical conductivity, this work establishes a general approach for freeform 3D soft electronics.

papers.title: Capsular Repair During Hip Arthroscopy for Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome Improves Revision Rates and Hip Outcome Score Result but Not Overall Patient‐Reported Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta‐analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials
papers.abstract: Purpose To determine whether capsular repair (CR) after hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome provides superior clinical outcomes, functional recovery, and complication profiles compared with nonrepair. Methods Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses guidelines, a search of PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and MEDLINE identified 5 randomized controlled trials comparing CR with no capsular repair in patients with femoroacetabular impingement. Studies published between 2000 and September 2025 with a follow‐up of ≥12 months were included. Data on patient demographics, surgical techniques, postoperative protocols, patient‐reported outcome measures, complications, and revision rates were extracted. Standardized mean differences were calculated using random‐effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q statistics and Higgins’ I 2 . Results Five randomized controlled trials (n = 615) met the inclusion criteria: 334 patients in the no capsular repair group and 281 in the CR group. Most patient‐reported outcome measures, including the modified Harris Hip Score, the International Hip Outcome Tool‐12, and all subscales of the Copenhagen Hip and Groin Outcome Score, showed no significant differences between groups. However, the Hip Outcome Score showed a significant advantage for CR (standardized mean difference = 0.59; P < .001). Revision procedures were more frequent in patients who did not undergo CR (15 vs 8 cases). Heterogeneity was generally low across analyses. Conclusions CR after hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome did not show significant advantages over nonrepair in most pooled patient‐reported outcome measures, including the modified Harris Hip Score, International Hip Outcome Tool‐12, and Hip and Groin Outcome Score subscales. However, CR was associated with superior Hip Outcome Score outcomes and lower rates of revision procedures and conversion to total hip arthroplasty. These differences were observed predominantly in studies including unrepaired T‐capsulotomy, whereas studies evaluating only interportal capsulotomy generally reported comparable outcomes between repair and nonrepair. Level of Evidence Level II, systematic review and meta‐analysis of Level I and II studies.

papers.title: THE ROLE OF INTERACTIVE METHODS IN DEVELOPING STUDENTS’ LINGUISTIC COMPETENCE IN MOTHER TONGUE LESSONS
papers.abstract: This theoretical and methodological study examines how interactive teaching methods can support the development of linguistic competence in mother tongue education. Drawing on Uzbek educational standards and international scholarship in sociocultural learning, communicative competence, formative assessment, cooperative learning and active learning, the article synthesizes mechanisms through which dialogue, problem-based tasks, peer interaction, language analysis and feedback can enhance grammatical awareness and functional language use. A structured narrative review and comparative pedagogical analysis were applied; no classroom experiment or learner-level quantitative dataset was collected. The results are presented as an evidence-informed instructional framework connecting specific interactive techniques with observable linguistic outcomes and assessment indicators. The framework emphasizes task authenticity, explicit linguistic objectives, accessibility, feedback quality and alignment with curriculum standards. Its proposed classroom application and evaluation criteria require subsequent empirical validation in Uzbek-language classrooms.

papers.title: Nuclear receptor NR4A1 enhances the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and improves TCP scaffold-mediated bone repair in mice.
papers.abstract: Functional reconstruction of calvarial defect is a considerable clinical challenge. Many studies have emphasized the osteogenic abilities of stem cells for tissue regeneration. Ttricalcium phosphate (TCP) has been employed successfully as a synthetic graft material in bone defect repair. However, the lack of osteogenic and osteoinductive properties of this substitute invariably results in bone regeneration of low quality and quantity. The purpose of this study was to determine whether loading NR4A1 gene-modified bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) onto TCP promoted bone regeneration and osteointegration of calvarial defect in mice. Alizarin red staining and qPCR were performed to investigate the influences of NR4A1 on osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and MC3T3-E1 cells. The effects of NR4A1 overexpressed BMSCs/TCP scaffold on osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs were assessed using Alizarin red staining, ALP staining and qPCR. To further evaluate the roles of NR4A1 overexpressed BMSCs/TCP scaffold in osteogenesis in vivo, we conducted animal experiments in mice. New bone formation was assessed using micro-CT and histological methods. In the present study, we found that NR4A1 promotes osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and MC3T3-E1 cells in vitro. Besides, NR4A1 overexpressed BMSCs/TCP scaffold showed stronger osteogenic differentiation ability than TCP scaffold in vitro. Finally, In vivo studies have shown that micro-CT and histology revealed significantly greater volume of new bone formation in the NR4A1 overexpressed BMSCs/TCP scaffold group than in the model group. HE staining of lung, liver, kindey and heart tissues showed that the TCP scaffold was not toxic to mice. These results demonstrated that combinations of TCP scaffolds and NR4A1 gene-modified BMSCs could be used to construct tissue-engineered bone to enhance mineralization of the regenerated bone and osseointegration in mice.

papers.title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Loco-manipulation, which requires mobile manipulators to coordinate locomotion and manipulation over long horizons, is a key capability for large-object rearrangement in applications such as service robotics and warehouse automation. Despite recent progress, reliably executing these tasks remains challenging because performance depends on complex robot-object and object-environment interaction dynamics. Existing approaches address this challenge either through model-based methods, which often require accurate dynamics models, or through learning-based methods, which reduce this requirement but typically assume a fixed or predefined initial grasp. However, different geometrically stable grasps can lead to substantially different downstream manipulation performance. Therefore, we propose Grasp-TAGS, a task-aware grasp selection framework for goal-conditioned large-object rearrangement. We train a unified PPO-based reinforcement learning policy across multiple initial grasp configurations and distill the learned critic into a lightweight grasp utility network that ranks candidate grasps using only the candidate grasp configuration and goal information. At inference time, we select the grasp with the highest predicted downstream utility for the downstream policy to complete the task, before even making a contact. Experiments demonstrate that Grasp-TAGS improves rearrangement success over both fixed single-grasp policies and random grasp selection, achieving an average success rate of 89.84% compared with 79.87% for the best-performing single-grasp policies, an improvement of 9.97 percentage points. Grasp-TAGS also reduces final orientation errors across all evaluated objects. For more qualitative results, refer to the supplementary webpage: https://rpm-lab-umn.github.io/Grasp-TAGS-web-page/

papers.title: The Cost of Coverage: Conformalising Native Forecast Uncertainty for GB Wind Power
papers.abstract: Uncertainty bands on wind forecasts help inform reserve sizing and commitments, but often fail to deliver their stated coverage. We apply conformal prediction to native bands to see what it adds and what it costs, comparing six forecasters, from ARIMA to a tabular foundation model, at two wind farms in Great Britain (GB) under operational conditions. We show that calibration repairs empirical marginal coverage with little or no Winkler Score penalty, but this apparent success conceals under-coverage in high winds. Calibrating by forecast wind regime turns marginal coverage into regime-level coverage, cutting day-ahead out-of-band volume in high winds by over 40% relative to pooled calibration while narrowing bands overall.

summary_zh.method: 对六种预测器的原生区间施加共形预测并按风况分层校准。
summary_zh.result: 分层校准修复了高风速下的欠覆盖，高风越界量降低逾40%。
summary_zh.validation: 英国两个风电场运行条件下的数值对比实验。

summary_en.motivation: Wind forecast uncertainty bands frequently fail to achieve their nominal coverage, undermining reserve sizing decisions.
summary_en.method: Conformal prediction is applied to native prediction intervals from six forecasters and calibrated both marginally and by forecast wind regime at two GB wind farms.
