papers.title: Autonomous Whole-body Loco-manipulation Using a Snake Robot
papers.abstract: Snake robots can leverage their hyper-redundant morphology for both locomotion and manipulation through distributed body contact but whole-body loco-manipulation is particularly challenging since the entire body serves simultaneously as propulsive mechanism and manipulation tool Prior work on wheeled legged and snake robot platforms has decoupled these functions through dedicated appendages body segmentation or grippers We present closed-loop loco-manipulation with our snake robot COBRA without this distinction such that any part of the body may make contact We develop a contact-implicit dynamic model unifying robot-ground robot-object and object-ground interactions within a Moreau-Jean time-stepping framework and formulate a trajectory optimization over the full-order dynamics guided by a geometric planner and nominal proportional controller to autonomously push an object to a goal location during sidewinding We validate the planner and controller on hardware across varied configurations and present simulation results for a simplified trajectory optimization that resolves robot-object and object-ground contacts

summary_en.validation: Hardware experiments on the COBRA robot plus simulation of a simplified trajectory optimization.

papers.title: ICare-DT: a digital twin for continuous forecasting of intensive care patients
papers.abstract: Digital twins of intensive care patients should update forecasts from new data and predict treatment responses, but few studies test whether routine records support either. We propose ICare-DT, a Transformer-based twin that updates a latent patient state hourly from new measurements without retraining. We trained it on 140,473 eICU-CRD stays to forecast vital signs crossing their training-set means. On test data, later forecasts beat the twin's own hour-6 forecasts of the same windows in all 12 settings (+0.073 to +0.153 AUROC). On validation data, controls that withheld or swapped the new hours traced the gain to the patient's own measurements. Without refitting, the model kept its gain on a second database (8 of 9 settings, +0.025 to +0.114 AUROC) in a prespecified evaluation of the previously analyzed MIMIC-IV test split. Refitted within MIMIC-IV, a twin state fine-tuned on clinical endpoints gave gradient boosting a significant gain for acute kidney injury (+0.0035 AUROC; hypotension +0.0010, not significant). To test response prediction, we built a benchmark that replaces the treatments in real records with simulated doses and injects responses of known size, visible only at measurement times. Ridge models supervised with injected effects recovered them from real records only through frequently measured variables (heart rate) read at their measurement times. We asked standard learners to predict these effects for a dosing regime no patient had received. No standard learner outperformed predicting zero effect at an out-of-support query. When told how the simulated responses were generated, a separate learner recovered the effects from the same records without seeing their true values (R2 0.30 to 0.40 at one effect size). Routine records support forecasts that improve with each patient's new data, and our benchmark is a testbed for models that learn how responses are generated.

papers.title: Autonomous Particle Image Velocimetry Using Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Particle image velocimetry (PIV) reconstructs a flow field from the motion of tracer particles but the reconstruction quality is bounded by how well the flow structure of interest is resolved in the images. The acquisition position is typically fixed by the operator before the measurement. We cast camera placement as a sequential decision-making problem and train a reinforcement learning agent to control a 6-DoF manipulator equipped with a camera, enabling it to locate, frame and resolve a hydrofoil wake in a water tunnel. The agent commands the camera pose and observes the scene only through the velocity field and uncertainty estimated from time-separated image pairs. It is trained entirely in a photorealistic simulation of our water tunnel, with wakes generated by Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations of hydrofoils with varying profiles, positions and angles of attack. After zero-shot transfer to the real water tunnel, the policy reliably locates and frames the wakes of randomly placed hydrofoils. It resolves the wake at a higher resolution than a fixed camera view and with lower error in the measured flow statistics, in roughly half the time of a full scan and with far fewer image pairs.

summary_en.motivation: PIV reconstruction quality is limited by the operator's fixed choice of acquisition viewpoint, motivating adaptive camera control.
summary_en.method: Camera placement is formulated as a sequential decision problem and a reinforcement learning policy for a 6-DoF manipulator is trained in a photorealistic water-tunnel simulation driven by CFD-generated hydrofoil wakes.
summary_en.result: The policy transfers zero-shot to the real tunnel, locating and framing randomly placed hydrofoil wakes at higher resolution and lower statistical error than a fixed view, in about half the scan time.
summary_en.validation: Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer is demonstrated experimentally in a physical water tunnel against a fixed-camera baseline.

papers.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) approaches have demonstrated strong performance across diverse domains in recent years, learning accurate world models from agent trajectories. However, despite this progress, current approaches still struggle to surpass human performance on tasks that require long-term memory and planning. In this work, we address the problem of long-term memory in MBRL by moving beyond the commonly studied paradigm of architecture design. We introduce Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (TT-MBRL), using gradient descent at test time to encode the memory of episode observations into world model parameters. This enables the agent to learn a distinct world model for each episode, improving memory capabilities compared to traditional approaches that solely rely on contextual memory. We first establish a proof of concept on a simplified two-dimensional variant of the Memory Maze environment, which we refer to as Memory Maze 2D, showing consistent improvements across different world model architectures. We then demonstrate the effectiveness of TT-MBRL in the 3D domain, achieving new state-of-the-art results on the Memory Maze benchmark. Finally, we show that TT-MBRL maintains strong performance on non-memory benchmarks such as DeepMind Control and Atari 100k.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究世界模型中的长期记忆机制，属于纯强化学习方法，与有限元代理建模、植入物生物力学设计无直接关联，仅可作为方法论背景参考。

summary_zh.result: 在Memory Maze 2D与3D基准上取得一致提升并刷新SOTA，在DMC与Atari 100k上保持强性能。
summary_zh.validation: 在Memory Maze、DeepMind Control与Atari 100k等仿真基准上评测。

summary_en.motivation: Model-based reinforcement learning still falls short of human-level performance on tasks demanding long-horizon memory and planning.
summary_en.method: The authors propose TT-MBRL, which performs gradient descent at test time to encode per-episode observations into world model parameters, yielding an episode-specific world model.
summary_en.result: The approach yields consistent gains across world model architectures, sets a new state of the art on Memory Maze, and retains strong performance on DeepMind Control and Atari 100k.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on simulated benchmarks including a 2D Memory Maze variant, the 3D Memory Maze, DeepMind Control, and Atari 100k.

papers.title: BiLoGo: Reducing the smoothing of localised responses in Transformer-based neural operators for sheet forming
papers.abstract: Trial-and-error FE simulation of sheet forming could be computationally expensive, neural-network-based learned simulators are used to accelerate design. These simulators should accurately capture localised responses, such as thinning around sharp radii or near ribs, which determine formability. Transformer-based neural operators propagate information efficiently across the mesh but tend to smooth such localised responses. This study develops BiLoGo, a Bipartite Local-Global learned simulator with an FE-guided design that connects local node-element message passing with a Transformer-based neural operator for long-range information exchange. BiLoGo has three modules: a bidirectional node-element GraphSAGE model that learns nodal-elemental coupling on a bipartite graph and predicts each quantity on its native FE entity without interpolation; a dual-stream Transformer-based neural operator that processes blank deformation and tool contact with separate token sets, preventing localised contact information from being averaged with the whole-blank state; and a fusion and element update module that combines global and local features via gated residual fusion and updates element features conditioned on element-node kinematics. Evaluated on a dome-shaped cold forming case and two corner-shaped hot stamping cases (one with ribs), BiLoGo achieves the lowest positional and threshold-based thinning errors on all three cases compared with single-level and hierarchical graph-based models and Transformer-based neural operators. Near the ribs, the smoothing index of predicted thinning increases from 0.41-0.56 for Transformer-based neural operators to 0.94 for BiLoGo-U. Compared with the hierarchical graph network CAtt-BiUGNN, BiLoGo-T reduces mean positional error by 15.5% on the Corner case and BiLoGo-U by 8.3% on the Corner+Rib case, with 66-69% less training memory.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文提出Transformer神经算子加速板材成形有限元仿真并改善局部响应平滑问题，其局部-全局耦合架构可迁移到植入物力学代理建模。
llm.why_not_core: It targets sheet metal forming FE simulation with no implant/biomechanics context, no uncertainty quantification, and no constrained design optimization.

summary_zh.result: 在三个成形案例上位置与减薄误差最低，肋区平滑指数由0.41-0.56升至0.94。
summary_zh.validation: 在穹顶冷成形与两个热冲压案例上与图网络及Transformer基线对比。

summary_en.method: A bipartite local-global simulator couples node-element GraphSAGE message passing with a dual-stream Transformer neural operator and gated residual fusion.
summary_en.result: The model attains the lowest positional and thinning errors across three forming cases and raises the near-rib smoothing index from 0.41-0.56 to 0.94.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on one dome cold-forming and two hot-stamping cases against single-level, hierarchical graph, and Transformer neural-operator baselines.

papers.title: Locally Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Polynomial Chaos Expansions
papers.abstract: This work develops a locally adaptive jackknife+ conformal prediction framework for polynomial chaos expansions. Therein, the non-conformity scores are normalized with an auxiliary polynomial chaos expansion trained on the log-transformed leave-one-out residuals of the base model. We show that the coverage guarantee of jackknife+ conformal prediction carries over to the adaptive intervals if the leave-one-out auxiliary models are trained on nested leave-one-out residuals. For fixed-basis polynomial chaos expansions fitted by ordinary least squares, all required quantities are derived in closed form and the guarantee-preserving adaptive intervals are obtained from a single model fit, without any model retraining. For sparse polynomial chaos expansions, where multiple model fits are necessary, we propose a heuristic simplification that limits the computational overhead of adaptivity at the cost of the formal coverage guarantee. Numerical experiments on an academic benchmark with known heteroscedastic noise and on an engineering simulation dataset show that the suggested method attains the target coverage while providing intervals that adapt to local prediction uncertainty, therefore being considerably more statistically efficient. These advantages are particularly prominent in high-uncertainty regions of the input space, where the performance of non-adaptive methods degrades substantially.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文为PCE代理模型提供局部自适应保形预测与覆盖率保证，可迁移到植入物/生物力学FEA代理建模的不确定性量化环节。
llm.why_not_core: It provides UQ for polynomial chaos surrogate predictions but contains no FEA of implant mechanics, no femoral stem stress shielding or bone-implant interface modeling, and no biomedical application.

summary_zh.motivation: 现有保形预测区间在输入空间高不确定区域过宽，统计效率低。
summary_zh.method: 用辅助PCE对留一残差取对数建模以归一化非一致性分数，实现局部自适应jackknife+区间。
summary_zh.result: 在异方差噪声基准与工程仿真数据上达到目标覆盖率，且区间更窄、统计效率更高。
summary_zh.validation: 在已知异方差噪声的学术基准和工程仿真数据集上做数值验证。

summary_en.method: Non-conformity scores are normalized by an auxiliary polynomial chaos expansion trained on log-transformed leave-one-out residuals, yielding locally adaptive jackknife+ intervals with closed-form quantities for fixed-basis OLS fits.
summary_en.result: The approach attains nominal coverage while producing substantially narrower, locally adaptive intervals, with the largest gains in high-uncertainty input regions.
summary_en.validation: Numerical experiments on an academic benchmark with known heteroscedastic noise and on an engineering simulation dataset.

papers.title: Active Learning of Robust Models
papers.abstract: In many domains from species identification to cancer diagnosis, labelling data to train predictive models remains costly. In these settings, it is advantageous to intelligently select data points to label to achieve the maximum information gain, this is the motivation behind the study of active learning. In addition to the high costs of acquiring data in such domains, there is the added complexity of data distribution shifts that can occur between training and deployment. For example, the features of cancerous skin cells taken in one country may be different in another region of the world. These two challenges - efficient labelling of data, and learning models robust to distribution shifts have been studied separately but not together, even though these challenges often co-occur in real-life settings. We identify failure modes of standard active learning approaches when the distribution of data at deployment is different from the distribution in which the data is sampled for labelling. We propose a new strategy for efficiently learning classifiers that generalise under specific forms of distribution shift, namely subpopulation shift. Drawing on work in learning from heterogeneous data, we aim to train models that perform well across subpopulations of the data, through active learning. To handle this challenging setting, we exploit the fact that many datasets include metadata about data collection that can serve as a noisy proxy for each sample's underlying subpopulation. We demonstrate how to leverage these noisy labels during active learning selection, and demonstrate empirically that our approach improves classifier accuracy across subpopulations.

summary_en.method: The authors exploit collection metadata as noisy proxies for latent subpopulations and incorporate them into the active learning selection criterion.
summary_en.result: Empirical results indicate improved classifier accuracy across subpopulations relative to standard active learning baselines.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated empirically on classification benchmarks exhibiting subpopulation shift.

papers.title: BEiTScore++: Reference-free Image Captioning Evaluation with BEiT-3 and Conformalized Quantile Regression
papers.abstract: Reliable uncertainty estimation is important for deploying evaluation metrics in real-world settings, where both input ambiguity and domain shifts are common. In this work, we propose an uncertainty-aware extension of the BEiTScore image captioning metric, producing conformally calibrated confidence intervals alongside alignment scores. Our approach models predictive distributions over human judgments, enabling both accurate scoring and principled uncertainty quantification in a single forward pass. We evaluate our BEiTScore++ metric across multiple benchmarks with human-annotated ratings, showing that it preserves the ranking correlation of BEiTScore, while producing intervals whose width tracks the prediction error more closely than Monte Carlo dropout on most benchmarks. The estimated uncertainty also grows under image degradation and on out-of-domain artwork images, making BEiTScore++ a practical tool for uncertainty-aware evaluation of image-caption alignment.

summary_zh.method: 基于BEiT-3建模预测分布，并用保形分位数回归校准置信区间。
summary_zh.result: 在保持排序相关性的同时，区间宽度更贴合预测误差。
summary_zh.validation: 在多个带人工评分的基准上对比MC dropout。

summary_en.motivation: Reliable uncertainty estimation is needed when deploying image-caption evaluation metrics under input ambiguity and domain shift.
summary_en.method: The authors extend the BEiTScore metric by modeling predictive distributions over human judgments and calibrating confidence intervals with conformalized quantile regression in a single forward pass.
summary_en.result: The proposed metric preserves BEiTScore's ranking correlation while yielding intervals whose width tracks prediction error more closely than Monte Carlo dropout on most benchmarks.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on multiple benchmarks with human-annotated ratings, including degraded and out-of-domain images.

papers.title: PhyCAD: Physics-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Language-driven computer-aided design (CAD) generation enables the creation of editable parametric models from text, yet geometric correctness alone does not ensure physical feasibility. We present PhyCAD, a framework for physics-aware Text-to-CAD generation that trains language models to produce executable CadQuery programs under geometric and physical constraints. To support this setting, we construct a Text-to-CAD dataset that links parametric CAD models with geometric specifications, loading conditions, and physical constraints. We further develop an automated CAD--CAE verifier that combines program execution, geometric checks, and finite element analysis to provide feedback for model training. A key learning challenge is to prioritize joint satisfaction of geometric and physical constraints while retaining informative feedback on partial progress. A flat aggregation of heterogeneous rewards can obscure this priority, allowing improvements in individual criteria to compensate for unmet design requirements. We therefore introduce a Hierarchical Balanced Advantage for Group Relative Policy Optimization, grouping candidates into levels according to their verification status and combining between-level progress with objective-wise peer ranking within each level. This formulation preserves cross-level priority in the training signal while providing fine-grained feedback for satisfying constraints and improving feasible designs. Experiments across multiple language models show that PhyCAD consistently improves joint geometric and physical constraint satisfaction. These results demonstrate the value of verifiable engineering feedback for advancing language-driven CAD generation beyond geometric reconstruction toward physics-aware design.

papers.title: k-Volume: a Unified Active Learning Strategy
papers.abstract: In the classification context where revealing the label of a sample is costly, we propose a new Active Learning (AL) strategy named k-Volume (kVol). It randomly selects a sample to be labeled according to the volume of the smallest ball containing its k nearest neighbors. kVol is highly versatile: it can be applied either in the input space or in the output space, and it enjoys the desirable properties of the three main families of AL strategies: density, diversity, and (when performed in the output space) uncertainty. From a theoretical perspective, we establish that kVol is asymptotically equivalent to uniform sampling over the support of the (input or output) data distribution. Based on experiments on various synthetic and real-life tabular datasets and images, we observe that kVol is surprisingly stable: whatever the classifier or the experimental setup, it still lies among the best AL strategies unlike other competitors that fail dramatically. In particular, kVol outperforms state-of-the-art competitors such as CoreSet, TypiClust or Uncertainty on several real-life datasets, at a low computational cost.

papers.title: Calibrated Uncertainty Quantification on TDC ADMET: What Can Be Resolved Across 22 Datasets?
papers.abstract: Absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) models often rely on small, heterogeneous datasets, yet their predictions may determine which compounds proceed to experimental testing. Useful evaluations must therefore assess both predictive performance and the quality of reported probabilities or intervals. We ask which common uncertainty-quantification methods perform best on the 22 Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC) ADMET datasets and what this benchmark can resolve. We compare eleven calibrated pipelines using nested five-fold cross-validation across ten chemical partitions and five model seeds. Ensemble Monte Carlo (MC) dropout has the best average rank for TDC performance, Brier score, and 90% interval score. For TDC performance, however, it is not separated from the other ensemble pipelines; for Brier and interval score, LightGBM is also not ruled out as best. LightGBM wins more individual datasets than any other method for TDC performance and Brier score, but performs poorly on several endpoints. Smaller evaluations can identify a different leader and often fail to recover the broader comparison. These results make LightGBM and an ensemble neural model complementary baselines. Comparative claims should be checked across multiple chemical partitions using statistical analyses matched to the question being asked.

papers.title: Probably Safe Sim-to-Real Transfer with Lifetime Validity
papers.abstract: We present Dejavu, a method that makes sim-to-real transfer of reinforcement learning policies in constrained Markov decision processes probably safe over an unbounded sequence of policy updates. An anytime valid test using per-decision importance sampling and a betting confidence sequence certifies each candidate trained in simulation before deployment using only trajectories collected by a safe baseline policy operating in production. Simulation quality does not affect the safety guarantee, only the production sample efficiency of the method. Finally, a summable per-test failure probability yields the lifetime valid property. Empirical results across three sim-to-real benchmarks support the theoretical work.

papers.title: A scaled TW-PINN framework for soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries equation
papers.abstract: Accurate approximation of soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation remains challenging for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) due to localized wave structures, high-order spatial derivatives, nonlinear interactions between solitons, and difficulties in long-time prediction. In this work, we address these challenges using a scaling PINN framework to approximate KdV soliton solutions. The framework transforms the governing equation into a normalized form, approximates its solution using a PINN solver, and reconstructs the solution in the original variables through inverse scaling. We introduce scaling transformations and PINN solvers tailored to one- and two-soliton problems. For the one-soliton case, we employ a PINN solver that incorporates a traveling-wave coordinate to capture soliton propagation. For the two-soliton case, we employ a two-step training procedure for the PINN solver. The first step learns the individual soliton profiles and estimates their propagation speeds, while the second step uses the estimated speeds to construct traveling-wave coordinates in the PINN solver and approximate the full two-soliton solution, including nonlinear interactions. We also introduce soliton-informed sampling (SIS), which places additional collocation points around the soliton trajectories. Numerical results show that the scaling PINN framework accurately captures one-soliton propagation, resolves two-soliton interactions, and preserves soliton profiles during long-time extrapolation in both cases. An additional three-soliton experiment suggests the applicability of the proposed two-step training procedure to multi-soliton solutions.

llm.why_not_core: It targets soliton solutions of the KdV equation with no FEA benchmark, no biomedical or implant mechanics context, no surrogate-based design optimization, and no uncertainty quantification.

summary_en.method: The governing equation is rescaled into a normalized form and solved with tailored PINN solvers that use traveling-wave coordinates, a two-step training scheme, and soliton-informed collocation sampling.
summary_en.result: The framework accurately reproduces one- and two-soliton dynamics, resolves nonlinear soliton interactions, and preserves soliton profiles under long-time extrapolation.

papers.title: Physics Informed Priors for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials with Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: Standard uncertainty quantification methods for machine learning interatomic potentials often fail to quantify the effects of model misspecification despite its prominence as a source of error. To combat this, misspecification-aware uncertainty schemes have been gaining attention, pointwise optimal parameter set regression (POPS-Regression) among them. However, no guarantees on the physicality of the posterior distribution are given and uncertainty estimates can be conservative compared to the true error. To combat this, we present a model misspecification aware scheme that builds on POPS-Regression by allowing users to specify physical priors that are enforced across the obtained ensemble of models. This allows the user to incorporate misspecification-aware uncertainties without compromising on physical properties. The scheme is applicable to any physical quantity that can be represented by a convex set of parameters and so is robust for a wide variety of static properties which can help inform dynamical simulations. Here, we demonstrate the scheme for phononic vibrations and elastic properties. The scheme is also applied to both linear and message-passing neural network potentials by exploiting the linearity available in both architectures; for neural network potentials we approximate the readout layer as a linear model based on fixed non-linear features. The versatility of the method provides an alternative to hand-crafted or active learning approaches to data-set construction to correct physical failures by adding data thus reducing the computational overhead for designing potentials for specific applications.

summary_en.result: The scheme yields misspecification-aware uncertainties that remain physically admissible for phononic and elastic properties.

papers.title: Towards an Autonomous AI Steward for Large-Scale Physics Experiments: Integrating Causal Diagnostics, RAG, and Conformal Prediction
papers.abstract: Long-term particle physics experiments face critical operational challenges: monitoring non-stationary machine data streams and preserving tacit expert knowledge. We present the "Helmholtz Co-Pilot," a hybrid Multi-Agent System (MAS) acting as an autonomous experiment steward. The system can be triggered interactively by human operators or autonomously by an asynchronous causal diagnostics engine that runs independently of the MAS reasoning core. Continuously monitoring live hardware streams such as data acquisition and slow control, this engine performs dynamic causal discovery to trace cascading alarms back to their root causes and applies adaptive model selection to keep forecasts reliable across shifting machine states; upon detecting an anomaly, it hands a structured diagnostic report to the MAS. The reasoning layer itself relies on a high-throughput C++ core and a Python edge architecture orchestrating a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of specialized ReAct workers. It integrates a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) backbone for institutional memory and leverages conformal prediction to bound its evidence-based recommendations with mathematical coverage guarantees. This extended abstract outlines the architecture, the integration of software-enforced Human-in-the-Loop (HitL) guardrails, and ongoing shadow-testing within the KATRIN experiment.

papers.title: SUGARv2: Learning Diverse Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Skills from Synthesized Interaction References
papers.abstract: Scaling up visual humanoid loco-manipulation skill acquisition requires reducing the human effort needed as tasks and spatial configurations expand, particularly in demonstration collection and task-specific training design. We present SUGARv2, a unified framework for learning diverse visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills through interaction reference synthesis and a shared training pipeline. To obtain diverse references at low cost, we adapt reusable task templates to different spatial configurations, synthesizing coordinated robot and object motions. To reduce task-specific reward design and training effort, we use reference-based imitation as a common learning objective across tasks. We first train privileged teachers to execute these references, then train visual policies through teacher distillation and reinforcement learning with the same reference-based mimic rewards, using diverse object instances and visual domain randomization to support visual generalization and sim-to-real transfer. Across five humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, SUGARv2 achieves a mean success rate of 91.0% in simulation. Deployment on a real humanoid robot further demonstrates successful sim-to-real transfer for whole-body manipulation. These results demonstrate the framework's potential for learning diverse visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills.

papers.title: Real-Time Nonlinear Mixed-Integer Model Predictive Control With Horizon-Tail Relaxations
papers.abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) of nonlinear systems with discrete decisions leads to mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) whose combinatorial complexity often prevents real-time deployment. In this paper, we propose a decomposition-based MPC method that reorders and reduces computations to shorten the delay between receiving a state measurement and applying the control input. Before the measurement arrives, we solve a continuous relaxation of the MINLP at a predicted state and construct a mixed-integer quadratic program (MIQP). Once the measured state is available, we solve the MIQP that reconstructs the discrete controls and simultaneously performs one sequential quadratic programming step toward the corresponding nonlinear solution. To reduce the combinatorial complexity in the horizon length, we either fix the integer controls or relax their integrality over the prediction horizon tail, while retaining an integer-feasible first control input. We derive error bounds relating the nonlinear objective values obtained with the horizon-tail approximations to the optimal value of the original mixed-integer problem. In a data center cooling example, the proposed method reduces mean feedback computation time by 94% relative to a state-of-the-art MINLP method with a total closed-loop cost difference of less than 1%.

summary_zh.method: 先对预测状态求连续松弛并构造MIQP，测量到达后求解MIQP并做一步SQP，同时用时域尾部松弛降低组合复杂度。

summary_zh.validation: 单一数据中心冷却仿真算例，并给出误差界推导。

papers.title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
papers.abstract: Foundation models increasingly guide robot actions, yet sustained autonomy requires efficient control and failure recovery. We introduce A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface. Learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals. MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. A correction encoder and adapter absorb this knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. The action model, A2-WLA, adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a vision-language-action policy. Surprisingly, this simple design with action pretraining and task specialization reaches 0.5755 Q-score on the 50-task BEHAVIOR 2026 public subset before online correction, 2.21x the 2025 winner's reported 0.2605 across different benchmark editions and training configurations. On all 100 BEHAVIOR 2026 public tasks, A2-MEAS achieves 0.6411 Q-score and 45.40% task success. On RoboTwin 2.0, A2-WLA achieves 93.98% average success, rising to 95.05% with the complete system. Across 12 real-robot tasks in five household settings, A2-WLA achieves 57.92% average success versus 26.67% for pi0.5. In long-horizon pour-over coffee preparation, a history-conditioned adapter raises post-failure completion at two filter-handling steps from 14% to 94% and from 8% to 82%, compared with A2-WLA retries. Our training infrastructure delivers 427.1 samples per second, 4.03x the throughput of a pi0.5 reference implementation on matched hardware. We will release the system, models, training scripts, and infrastructure to support efficient embodied learning.

papers.title: Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations
papers.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. Motivated by the principle of gradient equidistribution from the stretching approach in grid generation, which redistributes solution gradients to reduce functional complexity, we propose Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which incorporate learnable coordinate transformations to map the physical domain into a computational domain where the physical solutions become approximately affine, making them easier for neural networks to learn. We propose two constructions of the transformation: an explicit construction based on Majorants and an implicit construction based on invertable neural networks. Experimentally, the explicit construction can improve accuracy for PDEs with available explicit coordinate transformations, and the implicit construction can be combined with other advanced PINN models as an efficient plug-in module to improve performance across a range of challenging PDE benchmarks.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文提出可学习坐标变换以改善PINN对陡峭梯度解的逼近，方法可迁移至生物力学FEA代理建模，但未涉及植入物或约束优化。
llm.why_not_core: The paper only benchmarks PINNs on abstract PDEs with sharp gradients and provides no FEA validation, no biomedical or implant mechanics context, no uncertainty quantification, and no constrained design optimization.

summary_zh.method: 引入可学习坐标变换，将物理域映射到解近似仿射的计算域，含显式Majorant构造与可逆网络隐式构造。
summary_zh.result: 显式构造提升可解析变换PDE的精度，隐式构造可作为插件提升多种困难PDE基准表现。

papers.title: Function-Space Certification for Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Certifying the robustness and physical consistency of scientific machine-learning models ensures that their predictions remain reliable beyond the test set. For neural operators, which learn PDE solution operators by mapping infinite-dimensional function spaces, certification means establishing rigorous, domain-wide guarantees for their output functions. However, standard neural network (NN) verification methods are fundamentally designed for vector-to-vector mappings, and they can only certify neural operators at fixed grid resolutions and provide no guarantees over the entire domain or across another resolution. We close this gap by introducing a function-space certification framework that verifies neural operators across the entire continuous domain. We formulate interval bound propagation (IBP) and CROWN in function space, propagating upper and lower bound functions through each layer using rigorous numerical integration. In addition, we extend bound propagation to higher-order derivatives to certify PDE residuals and solution error bounds. Experiments across several neural operator architectures and scientific problems, including the 572.5-million-parameter spherical Fourier neural operator for global weather forecasting, show that our method produces tight, domain-wide guarantees efficiently, providing a foundation for trustworthy operator learning.

summary_en.result: The framework yields tight, domain-wide guarantees efficiently across several operator architectures and scientific problems, including a 572.5-million-parameter spherical Fourier neural operator for global weather forecasting.
summary_en.validation: Numerical experiments on multiple neural operator architectures and scientific PDE benchmarks.

papers.title: FASTFUNNELS: Agile Multi Robot Navigation in Narrow Spaces via Adaptive Dynamic Funnels
papers.abstract: We focus on the problem of high-speed multi-robot navigation in cluttered spaces with tight spatial constraints. A key challenge is balancing safety with agility, as existing methods often trade one for the other (slowing down near a bottleneck to avoid collisions versus failing to swerve in time at high speeds), especially for car-like systems. Our approach belongs to the family of formation control methods, in which Ackermann-steering agents coordinate while navigating tight spaces. However, current formation control techniques rely on rigid, pre-defined shapes and transitions that depend on initial conditions, the environment, and vehicle dynamics, and are impractical to maintain at high speeds. For example, agents passing through a small gap must first form a square, transform into a line using analytical equations, and then return to a square. In contrast, our approach is inspired by a droplet of water that continuously adapts its shape to the space it flows through without slowing down. We propose a hierarchical algorithm in which, at the high level, a reinforcement learning policy produces a dynamic, blob-like elliptical patch that morphs its shape in real time, squeezing, stretching, and orienting itself around obstacles and through tight spaces. At the low level, the robots are controlled via distributed model predictive control (DMPC) to stay inside the patch, which acts as a soft forcing function, while avoiding collisions with each other. We evaluate our approach, FastFunnels, on simulated F1TENTH racing cars across 14 scenarios with N=1 to N=6 robots, averaged over 20 trials each. FastFunnels achieves an 89% completion rate at 7.73 m/s, while all baselines either fail to complete the track or succeed only at very low speeds (0.07-1.79 m/s, about 40% completion rate).

summary_en.method: A hierarchical scheme where an RL policy generates a morphing elliptical patch and distributed MPC keeps Ackermann-steered agents within it while avoiding collisions.

papers.title: Concordance-Optimal Continuous Music Emotion Estimation: Variance Decomposition, Dual-Branch Temporal Fusion, and Conformal Prediction Intervals
papers.abstract: Continuous music emotion recognition (MER) estimates how Arousal and Valence evolve within a song, yet the field's standard metric, pooled frame-level correlation, is dominated by between-song differences and cannot distinguish a model that tracks emotional dynamics from one that only ranks songs by their average level. We decompose annotation variance into between- and within-song components and show that mean squared error (MSE) targets the former, while windowed Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC = $r \cdot C_b$) targets the latter by penalising the variance compression MSE induces. A single weight $λ$ controls the trade-off: on 1,764 DEAM songs, raising $λ$ from 0 to 1 lowers pooled Arousal $r$ from 0.843 to 0.810 while raising mean within-song $r$ from 0.204 to 0.368.   Building on this objective, we present MMAS (Multimodal Music Analysis System), an open-source model that predicts Arousal and Valence every 0.5 s from raw audio. It fuses frozen MERT-v1-95M embeddings with ten symbolic features from automatic transcription through a dual-branch temporal convolutional network with cross-modal attention. Because both branches are audio-derived, one model trains jointly on DEAM and PMEmo without domain conditioning. Under song-grouped 5-fold cross-validation (2,531 songs), pooled $r$ reaches 0.801/0.685 (Arousal/Valence) on DEAM and 0.742/0.746 on PMEmo. Against a ridge baseline on identical features, within-song Arousal $r$ roughly triples (0.344 vs. 0.125; $n = 353$ songs, Wilcoxon $p = 1.7 \times 10^{-21}$, $d = 0.56$). Complete transcription failure costs at most 0.04 pooled $r$. Split-conformal intervals attain 93.7% (Arousal) and 90.0% (Valence) marginal coverage at a 95% target, with the shortfall traced to within-song dependence. MMAS is released as a pip-installable package.

papers.title: FATHOM: World-Model-Guided Diffusion Action-Trajectory Selection for Sparse-Marker AUV Tracking
papers.abstract: Reliable relative tracking is fundamental to cooperative autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), yet remains challenging under nonlinear vehicle dynamics and degraded underwater visual conditions. Active light markers improve robustness to appearance variation, but provide deliberately sparse observations that can become incomplete or corrupted by occlusion, reflections, and detection noise during dynamic motion. To address the resulting partial-observation control problem, this paper proposes FATHOM, a world-model-guided diffusion action-trajectory selection framework for sparse-marker AUV tracking. FATHOM first integrates structured marker observations, inertial measurements, action history, and temporal dynamics into a predictive tracking belief using a multimodal task-supervised recurrent state-space model. A diffusion action prior then generates multiple expert-like multi-thruster trajectories, whose future tracking consequences are predicted through the learned latent dynamics. Rather than directly executing a generated trajectory, FATHOM selects the most favorable candidate under an explicit receding-horizon objective and continually updates the decision from onboard observations. Extensive offline analyses verify the learned predictive belief, multi-step world-model prediction, diffusion trajectory generation, and predictive selection. More importantly, comprehensive real-AUV experiments, including strong pose-based comparisons and component ablations, demonstrate robust autonomous tracking across nominal and challenging motions with naturally occurring partial marker visibility, while maintaining real-time onboard operation without motion-capture feedback.

papers.title: Lodos: A Lightweight Simulator Designed for Contact-Rich Interactions with Detailed Meshes
papers.abstract: In recent years, massively parallelized rigid-body simulation has played a central role in robotics research, enabling rapid progress in areas such as reinforcement learning, stochastic optimal control, and randomized smoothing-based trajectory optimization. Particularly in contact-rich settings, the scalability of such simulations in large part depends on well-optimized representations of collision geometry, often requiring a coarse approximation of the underlying surfaces using primitives such as spheres, capsules, cylinders, and boxes. Whenever the complexity of the surfaces or the precision demands of the application render such approximations insufficient, it is instead necessary to employ mesh-mesh collisions, which impose a significant reduction in throughput. This paper proposes a simulation framework designed from scratch to address this bottleneck, with novel routines for broadphase and narrowphase collision detection as well as the subsequent contact dynamics computation. As experimentally validated, the framework matches existing well-established simulators in terms of physical faithfulness, and can achieve approximately an order of magnitude higher throughput in the detailed mesh-mesh collision setting that it specializes in. The source code is available at https://github.com/martius-lab/lodos.

papers.title: STRIDE: Learning Humanoid Locomotion in Minutes with Acceleration-Based Rewards
papers.abstract: Learning locomotion directly on a humanoid robot is a promising direction to avoid the sim-to-real gap. However, locomotion rewards in Reinforcement Learning (RL) typically track the base velocity, which cannot be measured onboard without an external motion capture system or well-calibrated state estimator. This is why we introduce \method{}, which learns humanoid locomotion from minutes of samples with a reward that only requires the onboard Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU). Instead of tracking the base velocity, STRIDE rewards the robot for following a commanded acceleration profile. To learn efficiently from this reward, we use the off-policy RL algorithm XQC and combine a high gain setting for the joint position controllers with left-right symmetry augmentation. In simulation, STRIDE learns to walk on the Unitree G1 and Booster T1 humanoids within 14 minutes of samples. Compared to learning without these two components, it reduces the falls during training by 81%, while without them the robot learns only in over an hour.

papers.title: It Takes Two to Tangram: Multi-Agent Object Centric Reinforcement Learning for Assembly
papers.abstract: Geometric assembly requires fine spatiotemporal coordination to place parts without causing collisions or deadlocks under tight clearances. To address this, we present an object-centric reinforcement learning framework that treats each part as an agent and learns a shared policy for continuous assembly control. A graph neural network represents the pieces, their target poses, and their spatial relationships, and predicts translational and angular velocities for each component. Per-agent proximal policy optimization with a centralized graph critic directly learns motion and temporal coordination within a single feedback policy. We study this formulation through planar Tangram assembly, where pieces must slide and rotate into a given configuration while remaining on the assembly surface. Procedural generation of target configurations and randomized initial arrangements support training and evaluation across diverse assembly problems. Our experiments isolate the roles of relational structure and multi-agent optimization, and compare learned control with sampling-based planning. We demonstrate concurrent assembly in simulation and transfer the policy to sequential execution on a real robot, as our object-centric formulation decouples learned assembly coordination from low-level physical control. Project page: https://tangrambench.org/

papers.title: Effect of low-level laser photobiomodulation on dental implant primary stability and postoperative pain: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Introducción: la fotobiomodulación es una técnica coadyuvante que promueve la oseointegración, procesos de cicatrización y disminuye l dolor postoperatorio mediante luz de baja intensidad para mejorar la estabilidad y recuperación en implantes dentales. Objetivo: evaluar el efecto de la fotobiomodulación con láser de baja intensidad sobre la estabilidad primaria de los implantes dentales (ISQ) y la reducción del dolor (EVA) mediante una Revisión Sistemática. Métodos: se realizó una búsqueda en PubMed, Cochrane, Scopus, LILACS y Google Scholar entre 2014 hasta abril de 2025. Se incluyeron ensayos clínicos aleatorizados (ECA) con aplicación de fotobiomodulación versus grupos control en pacientes adultos con implantes dentales. Se evaluó el ISQ y el dolor postoperatorio. Dos investigadores obtuvieron los datos, evaluaron el riesgo de sesgo mediante RoB 2 y realizaron una síntesis narrativa estructurada (SWiM). Resultados: se identificaron 131 registros, de los cuales 11 estudios se incluyeron, con un total de 278 pacientes. La longitud de onda en el infrarrojo (780-980 nm) con láser de diodo GaAlAs fue utilizada en el 81.8%. El ISQ en los grupos tratados con fotobiomodulación se concentraron en estabilidad media-alta (≥60) en el 63.6 %, y el dolor postoperatorio se mantuvo en niveles mínimos (EVA 0-2) en un 75 %. El riesgo de sesgo fue de algunas preocupaciones a bajo riesgo en todos los estudios. Conclusión: la fotobiomodulación con láser de diodo en el infrarrojo, aplicada en el periodo postoperatorio, se asocia con mayor estabilidad primaria de los implantes y una reducción significativa del dolor postoperatorio.

papers.title: Efecto de la fotobiomodulación con láser de baja intensidad en la estabilidad primaria de implantes dentales y el dolor postoperatorio: una revisión sistemática
papers.abstract: Introduction: Photobiomodulation (PBM) is an adjunctive technique that promotes osseointegration and healing processes, and reduces postoperative pain, using low-intensity light to improve stability and recovery in dental implants. Objective: To evaluate the effect of low-level laser photobiomodulation (PBM) on dental implant primary stability (ISQ) and pain reduction (VAS) through a systematic review. Methods: A search was conducted across PubMed, Cochrane, Scopus, LILACS, and Google Scholar covering the period from 2014 to April 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the application of fotobiomodulation against control groups in adult patients with dental implants were included. ISQ and postoperative pain were evaluated. Two researchers extracted the data, assessed the risk of bias using RoB 2, and performed a structured synthesis without meta-analysis (SWiM). Results: A total of 131 records were identified, of which 11 studies involving 278 patients were included. Infrared wavelengths (780–980 nm) using GaAlAs diode lasers were employed in 81.8% of cases. In the groups treated with PBM, ISQ values fell within the medium-to-high stability range (≥60) in 63.6% of cases, and postoperative pain remained at minimal levels (VAS 0–2) in 75%. The risk of bias across all studies ranged from "some concerns" to "low risk.". Conclusions: Infrared diode laser-assisted PBM, applied in the postoperative period, is associated with greater primary implant stability and a significant reduction in postoperative pain.

papers.title: PENERAPAN MODEL TEAMS GAMES TOURNAMENT (TGT) DENGAN MEDIA FRACTION CHAMPIONS UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KEAKTIFAN BELAJAR MATEMATIKA MATERI PERKALIAN PECAHAN DENGAN BILANGAN ASLI SISWA KELAS VIB SDN DAYA 1
papers.abstract: This study aimed to improve students’ learning activeness in mathematics, particularly in multiplying fractions by whole numbers, through the implementation of the Teams Games Tournament (TGT) cooperative learning model assisted by Fraction Champions among Class VIB students at SDN Daya 1. Fraction Champions is a learning medium consisting of question cards displayed one at a time by the teacher and answered competitively by student groups. This study employed a Classroom Action Research (CAR) design conducted in two cycles involving 20 students. Data were collected using an observation sheet covering five indicators of learning activeness and were analysed descriptively and quantitatively. The results showed that the percentage of overall classroom activeness increased from 60.5% in the pre-cycle to 75% in Cycle I and 81.5% in Cycle II. The number of students meeting the active learning criteria also increased from 6 students (30%) in the pre-cycle to 13 students (65%) in Cycle I and 17 students (85%) in Cycle II. Furthermore, the total number of correct answers given by all groups during the Fraction Champions game increased from 30 in Cycle I to 42 in Cycle II. These findings indicate that the TGT cooperative learning model assisted by Fraction Champions can serve as an alternative approach to improving students’ learning activeness in mathematics, particularly in multiplying fractions by whole numbers.

papers.title: PENINGKATAN KEAKTIFAN BELAJAR MURID PADA PEMBELAJARAN MATEMATIKA KELAS III UPT SPF SDN DAYA 1 DENGAN PENDEKATAN TEACHING AT THE RIGHT LEVEL (TaRL)
papers.abstract: Active learning is one of the key aspects of mathematics instruction in elementary school, particularly in fostering student engagement in understanding concepts and solving problems. This study aims to enhance students’ active learning through the application of the Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) approach in mathematics instruction on the topic of adding whole numbers up to 100. This study employs the Classroom Action Research (CAR) method based on Kurt Lewin’s model, which includes the stages of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The research subjects consisted of 26 third-grade students at UPT SPF SD Negeri Daya 1. The study was conducted in September 2026 over two cycles, with each cycle comprising two sessions. Data were collected through tests, observations, and documentation, then analyzed using descriptive quantitative and qualitative methods. The results showed that the average student learning engagement increased from 51.28% in Cycle I to 78.21% in Cycle II, representing a 26.93% increase. Improvements were observed across all learning engagement indicators, with the largest increase—38.46%—in the indicator of asking questions to the teacher or peers. In Cycle II, all indicators reached the “at least good” category, thus fulfilling the criteria for research success. Consequently, the implementation of the TaRL approach—accompanied by adjustments to the worksheets and individualized support based on students’ initial abilities—can enhance learning engagement in third-grade elementary school mathematics instruction.

papers.title: Adaptive Intelligence for Electric Vehicle–Microgrid Interaction Under Renewable Uncertainty
papers.abstract: An adaptive intelligence system has been developed to allow coordinated interactions between electric vehicles (EVs) and renewable-powered microgrids in the presence of high uncertainty. The proposed approach utilizes a combination of hybrid reinforcement learning and model predictive control to dynamically schedule EV charging and discharging to meet demand locally, maximize use of renewable resources, and provide ancillary services while taking into account battery constraints and user preferences. A probabilistic forecasting component is used to model uncertainty in renewable generation, feeding adaptive policies that update in real time; these adaptive policies will provide the corresponding EVs with updated scheduling information relative to their charging or discharging times. Simulations performed on a representative microgrid have demonstrated increased reliability, reduced energy costs, and decreased greenhouse gas emissions compared to traditional dispatch approaches. The adaptability of the framework allows it to scale to varied fleet sizes and levels of renewable penetration, while remaining robust to errors in forecasting and delays in communication. Contributions of this research include a modular adaptive control architecture, uncertainty-aware decision-making rules, and performance benchmarks that demonstrate the existing trade-offs between cost, degradation of batteries, and quality of service. Practical considerations for implementation of the proposed solution are presented along with future research directions and implementation challenges.

papers.title: Currículo em Ação e Formação Docente: uma experiência de articulação de contextos curriculares na licenciatura em pedagogia
papers.abstract: Resumo Este artigo versa sobre a integração curricular na formação inicial de professores de Licenciatura em Pedagogia em uma universidade paulistana, propondo uma categoria analítica emergente, de natureza relacional, para compreender processos colaborativos de integração curricular. A atividade foi realizada por meio da Metodologia da problematização, a partir do Arco de Maguerez, e articula a teoria e a vivência prática no contexto de estágio dos estudantes. Com abordagem qualitativa e análise retrospectiva e interpretativa, a análise dos dados sugere que a articulação de contextos curriculares se configura como um dispositivo capaz de integrar teoria e prática, fortalecer a colaboração docente e processos de aprendizagem situada na formação inicial de professores. Palavras-chave: formação de professores; currículo; educação superior; prática docente; metodologias ativas. Abstract This article addresses curricular integration in the initial teacher training of Pedagogy students at a university in São Paulo, proposing an emerging, relational analytical category to understand collaborative processes of curricular integration. The activity was conducted using the "problematization methodology", based on the Maguerez Arc, and links theory with practical experience within the students' internship context. Employing a qualitative approach and a retrospective, interpretive analysis, the findings suggest that linking curricular contexts serves as a mechanism capable of integrating theory and practice, as well as strengthening teacher collaboration and situated learning processes in initial teacher education. Keywords: teacher education; curriculum; higher education; teacher practice; active learning. Resumen Este artículo aborda la integración curricular en la formación inicial de profesores de la Licenciatura en Pedagogía de una universidad de São Paulo, proponiendo una categoría analítica emergente, de naturaleza relacional, para comprender los procesos colaborativos de integración curricular. La actividad se llevó a cabo mediante la metodología de la problematización, a partir del Arco de Maguerez y articuló la teoría y la experiencia práctica en el contexto de las prácticas de los estudiantes. Con un enfoque cualitativo y un análisis retrospectivo e interpretativo, el análisis de los datos sugiere que la articulación de contextos curriculares se configura como un dispositivo capaz de integrar teoría y práctica, fortalecer la colaboración docente y los procesos de aprendizaje situado en la formación inicial del profesorado. Palabras-clave: formación del profesorado; currículo; educación superior; práctica docente; metodologías activas.
